Rising Penetration in BBU Adoption Driven by Higher Power Density
We estimate BBU penetration in AI racks would rise from 10-15% in 2023-2024 to
40-45% in 2025, 60-65% in 2026, >85% in 2027. This estimate is based on the
evolution of AI rack architecture along with our industry checks, the transition from
traditional server racks to rack-scale systems such as GB200/300 NVL72, and the

growing adoption of OCP ORv3 power architecture.
n2023-2024 (10-15% of penetration) early adoption stage
Most AI infrastructure deployed during this period was still based on H100/200-
class system and more traditional data center power architecture. Backup power
was generally handled at the facility level through centralized UPS systems rather
than distributed at the rack level.
n2025 (40-45% of penetration) rising with GB200 NVL72
The key change is GB200 NVL72 is a rack-scale system that integrates multiple

compute trays, switch trays, liquid cooling, power shelves and high speed NVLink
connectivity into a single rack-level platform, which changes the way power
backup needs to be designed. As rack power moves toward 100KW+ range, BBU,
which is more space saving, has less distribution losses and higher flexibility,
becomes more ideal to support short-duration backup power closer to the IT load.
We thus believe BBU adoption rate should start rising meaningfully in particular

among hyperscalers who adopt OCP ORv3-style racks, pursuing higher power
efficiency or want to reduce reliance on large centralized UPS systems.
n2026 (60-65% of penetration) broader adoption with GB200/300 and ORv3
architecture
Few drivers in this stage include 1) AI rack power density continues to rise. Higher
rack power makes short-duration ride through protection more important. 2) OCP
ORv3 defines a BBU shelf architecture, with BBU shelf connected to the rack-level

DC bus. We believe large CSPs with strong in-house infrastructure teams would
adopt BBU more aggressively.
n2027 (>85%) BBU becomes a must for HVDC AI racks
We believe the transition toward HVDC power architecture could further accelerate
BBU adoption. Under HVDC architecture, the datacenter increasingly distributes
high-voltage DC power directly to the rack. Once the rack is operating on a DC
backbone, it becomes more natural to connect battery-based backup power

directly to the DC bus. Thie reduces the need for multiple ACDC and DCAC
conversion stage and improves the efficiency of short-duration backup power
delivery. We thus expect a growing share of high-density AI racks will adopt either
in-rack BBU shelves or sidecar/power rack BBU.

positioned to capture rising BBU demand as AI server racks move to higher power 
density. As rack-level power consumption moves toward >100kW and future 
platforms require even higher power density, datacenters need faster and more 
localized backup power solutions. We expect BBU adoption to rise with 
OCP/HVDC power architecture evolution, while higher rack power should also 
drive higher BBU content value per rack. We forecast sales to rise 34% CAGR in 
2025-2028E, boosted by strong non-IT sales +74% CAGR. 
Margin expansion from rising non-IT mix — Dynapack’s legacy IT battery 
business is mature and faces pricing pressure. We estimate IT battery pack GPM at 
only 5-10%. By contrast, BBU products require customized design, higher reliability 
standards, stricter safety validations and closer collaboration with PSU operators 
and CSPs. We estimate BBU GPM at 30-35%, materially above legacy IT products. 
As Dynapack shifts toward higher margin BBU products, we forecast GPM to 
expand from 16.6% in 2025 to 22.2% in 2026E, 26.0% in 2027E and 28.4% in

PSU partnerships broaden CSP exposure — We think Dynapack’s partnership 
model with PSU operators is a key strategic advantage. PSU operators typically 
control power shelves, rack level power architecture and system level customer 
interface; whereas Dynapack focuses on the battery pack layer where it has strong 
knowhow in battery design, BMS management and customized manufacturing. By 
working with multiple PSU operators, Dynapack can indirectly access a broader 
CSP and AIDC customer base, reducing reliance on any single CSP or platform.

capacity expansion. Our target P/E of 32x is based on our forecast EPS CAGR of

major PSU partner, as we expect Dynapack to grow alongside Delta.

Dynapack (3211.TWO): Our
Investment Thesis
Investment positive #1 – riding on the strong demand of
BBU from AIDC buildout, driving structural growth
Dynapack has historically been a notebook and consumer electronic battery-pack
supplier, but its product portfolio is increasingly expanding into non-IT
applications such as BBU, UPS, ESS, and LEV battery packs. Among these, BBU is

the most important structural growth opportunity for Dynapack, making up the
majority of its non-IT sales.  We estimate BBU sales to contribute 35% of
Dynapack’s group sales in 2025 and accelerate to 55% of group sales in 2026E.
We believe Dynapack is well positioned to benefit from rising BBU demand driven
by AIDC infrastructure buildout. As AI server racks move from traditional low-
power racks to high-density GPU racks, rack level consumption is increasing

significantly.
This creates a greater need for localized backup power solutions that can provide
immediate power support during grid instability, power transition, or short-
duration outages. As indicated in the industry section, unlike traditional
centralized UPS systems, BBU can be deployed closer to the server rack or power
shelf, enabling faster responses, lower conversion loss, and better compatibility
with high-density rack-scale power architectures.

We expect when the rack power is moving towards >150KW levels, BBU is likely to
become an increasingly important component in AI rack power architecture, as
higher rack power density raises both the absolute amount of backup power
required per rack and the fast load transients.

For Dynapack, BBU provides a meaningful growth opportunity beyond its mature
consumer electronic battery-pack business. Dynapack has long-standing
experience in lithium-ion battery pack design, battery management systems,
safety certifications, and customized manufacturing.
We think Dynapack’s BBU opportunity is not only a volume growth story but also a
content value expansion story – as AI rack power rises, the required backup power

per rack should increase, suggesting higher BBU content value per rack over time.
Furthermore, we’ve seen a clear trend that future AI power architecture would shift
from centralized UPS toward more distributed BBU deployment at the shelf, rack,
or DC busway level, which could structurally lift BBU penetration in AI datacenters.
We believe that as AI rack shipment continues to scale and BBU adoption rises with
OCP/HVDC power architecture evolution, Dynapack is poised to benefit from both

higher non-IT sales contribution and better product mix.

What Are Dynapack’s Competitive Advantages vs. Other BBU suppliers?
1.Strong battery-pack know-how – it has a long operating history as a

lithium-ion battery-pack maker, specializing in pack design, cell
integration, battery management, safety validation, and customized
manufacturing.
2.Strong partnership with PSU operators – unlike Panasonic or AES who
rely mostly on direct engagement with a single CSP or a narrow set of end
customers, working with PSU companies allows Dynapack to gain access
to a broader set of CSPs.
3.Faster capacity ramp-up to capture near-term strong BBU demand –

compared with other BBU suppliers that may need to squeeze new
production lines into existing facilities or secure new land and construct
new facilities, Dynapack appears to have more flexibility to expand
capacity as they have self-owned facility space in Taiwan, which allows
them to accelerate capacity addition. The mgmt. expects non-IT capacity
to be 2x more by end-2026 vs. end-2025.

Investment positive #2 – Intact margin expansion from
rising non-IT sales
We expect Dynapack to enjoy intact margin expansion trajectory in the coming
years, supported by rising contribution from non-IT products, in particular, BBU.
The company’s legacy IT battery pack business is mature with more intense pricing
pressure from notebook and consumer electronics customers. As a result, we

estimate GPM of IT battery pack to be only 5-10%, benchmarked with Dynapack’s
group GPM in 2016-2023 before BBU started becoming the key sales driver.
In contrast, BBU products are still in an early growth stage and require highly
customized designs, higher reliability standards, stricter safety validation, and
closer collaboration with PSU operators and CSPs. We estimate BBU GPM to be
30-35%, benchmarked with AES’s GPM, materially higher than the legacy IT

business. Unlike notebook battery packs, where the market is mature and
customers have stronger bargaining power, we believe AIDC BBU is a higher spec
product category with a higher entry barrier, supporting better pricing power.

Investment positive #3 – Strong Partnership with PSU
operators provides access to a broader CSP base
We believe Dynapack’s partnership with PSU operators is a key strategic advantage
in the AIDC BBU supply chain. Dynapack appears to be positioning itself as a
specialized BBU battery pack partner to power supply companies. The model is
strategically attractive because PSU operators typically control the power shelf,

rack-level power architecture and system level customer interface, while Dynapack
can focus on the battery pack where it has stronger know-how in Lithium-ion pack
design, BMS, thermal management, safety validations and customized
manufacturing.
This partnership model allows Dynapack to gain access to a broader downstream
customer base. Major PSU operators usually serve multiple CSPs, ODMs, and AI
server programs. By working with more than one PSU customer, Dynapack can

participate in multiple end-customer projects, creating a more balanced customer
mix over time.
We believe this is especially important in the early stage of the AI BBU market,
where rack power architecture is still evolving and customer specifications differ
across different generations of architecture. A supplier engaged in a couple of PSU
platforms should be better positioned to capture industry-wide BBU adoption
than a vendor tied to only one CSP .

We also think PSU operators would have strong incentives to work with specialized
BBU pack suppliers instead of fully internalizing the battery-packs as PSU vendors’
core strength is power conversion, rectifiers, power shelves, rack-level distribution
and system integration. In contrast, BBU pack manufacturing requires a different
capability set, including cell matching, battery management, thermal protection,
and safety certifications etc. Given the safety sensitivity of lithium-ion batteries

inside datacenters, PSUs are likely to prefer qualified BBU partners that can reduce
engineering burden and lower certification risks. Whereas for Dynapack, this
creates a share gain opportunity as the company can benefit from the scale and
customer access of PSU operators, growing with PSUs as BBU adoption rises
across AI racks. This complementarity should make the relationship structurally
more sustainable, in our view.
As BBU demand accelerates with higher AI rack power density, PSU operators will

need suppliers that can provide both engineering customization and volume
production. We believe Dynapack’s long history in battery-pack manufacturing,
customized BBU product development, and aggressive capacity expansion should
strengthen its leading position as a preferred partner.

Would PSU Operators Fully Vertically Integrate into BBU Manufacturing and
Compete with Specialized BBU Vendors?
We think the risk is relatively low as BBU requires a very different technical
capability set from traditional power conversion. The core advantage of PSU

vendors such as Delta and Lite-on lies in rectifiers, power conversion, rack/shelf-
level power distribution, and most importantly, system integration. Whereas, BBU
pack manufacturing requires deep know-how in lithium-ion cell
selection/matching, pack design, BMS, thermal management, safety protection,
and reliability validation.
We believe safety is one of the most important barriers – Li-on BBU products must
meet strict safety and reliability requirements involving multiple dedicated testing

and certification across battery safety standards. For example, UL 9540A, a fire-
testing method evaluating thermal runaway behavior and fire propagation risk.
Therefore, PSU operators are more likely to retain control of the system
architecture and customer interface, while collaborating with qualified BBU
vendors such as Dynapack. This allows PSU operators to shorten development
cycles, avoid heavy capex and learning curve costs and maintain focus on their

higher-value power system integration role.

Dynapack (3211.TWO): Financial
Analysis
Income Statement Analysis
Dynapack’s revenue fell over 2022-2025 as weakness in its mature IT battery-
pack business more than offset the still-early contribution from non-IT products.
Net sales fell from NT$19.1bn in 2022 to NT$13.2bn in 2025, implying a 2022-
2025 sales CAGR of -11.5%. This reflects soft notebook demand, pricing pressure

in legacy IT battery packs and the fact that BBU/UPS/ESS revenue had not yet
reached sufficient scale to offset the IT downturn.
Thanks to the strong BBU demand for AIDC applications, the group quarterly sales
had turned to positive growth starting from 3Q25. We forecast revenue growth to
accelerate meaningfully from 2026E, driven by the ongoing ramp-up of BBU
products for AIDC, rising rack power density leading to higher penetration of BBU,
and its share gains. We expect the legacy IT battery pack business to remain

mature.
We estimate sales to grow 35% y/y in 2026E, followed by 35% y/y in 2027E and
33% y/y in 2028E, implying a 2025-2028E sales CAGR of 34%.

Balance Sheet and Cash Flow Analysis
We expect Dynapack’s balance sheet to remain healthy through the BBU ramp-up
cycle, with the company staying in a net cash position despite higher working
capital needs and capacity expansion. Based on our estimate, cash and cash

equivalent stay at 20-31% in 2026-2028E vs. 2025’s 27%. This provides sufficient
liquidity to support BBU capacity expansion, inventory preparation and product
development for higher-power BBU products.
Net gearing remains negative throughout our forecast period, indicating that the
company maintains a net cash balance. We believe that their capacity expansion is
not overly dependent on external financing and the company still has room to fund
capacity ramp-up while maintaining balance sheet flexibility.

Dynapack’s cash conversion lowered to 55 days in 2025, down from 2022’s 86
days. We forecast it to further improve to 48 days in 2026E and 38 days in 2027E.
This improvement is mainly supported by stronger payable days and better
inventory discipline.

Dynapack (3211.TWO): Valuation
Methodology and Risks
We value Dynapack based on target P/E as we believe earnings growth, margin
expansion and the company’s positioning in AI datacenter BBU supply chain will be
the key focus areas for the market.
We use 2027E as our valuation base, as we believe 2027E would better reflect the
company’s earnings power after BBU capacity expansion. We apply a target P/E of

32x to our 2027E EPS of NT$25.0, and derive our target price of NT$800. Our
target P/E of 32x is based on our forecast EPS CAGR of 66% over 2025-2027E and
a PEG of 0.5x, benchmarked against Delta, its major PSU partner, as we expect
Dynapack to grow alongside Delta.
Our target P/E of 32x is also close to the high end of historical forward P/E range of
14-31x since the stock re-rated in 2025, which we view as justified in view of
Dynapack’s exposure to secular AI datacenter power demand, potential BBU

content value increase, margin expansion from higher non-IT sales, and improving
ROE.
Before BBU started to become a key growth driver in 2024, Dynapack was trading
at an average of 14x forward P/E, which reflected the soft outlook and rising
competition of its legacy business. In 4Q24-1H26, the company was trading at 20x
on average, thanks to the strong BBU demand, driving strong sales and earnings.
We believe Dynapack is likely to re-rate from its historical valuation range,

supported by its transition from a mature IT battery pack supplier to an AIDC BBU
beneficiary and aggressive capacity expansion, driving strong margin expansion
and robust earnings momentum.

Key Downside Risks to Our Price Target/Rating Are:
1.Slower-than-expected BBU adoption in AIDC: If CSPs continue to rely
mainly on centralized UPS, adopt only partial BBU deployment, or delay

rack-level BBU implementation due to cost, safety or system design
considerations.
2. Delay in PSU customer qualifications: The company’s BBU growth
depends heavily on qualification with PSU operators and downstream
CSP programs. Any delay in PSU platform qualification or CSP validation
could push revenue recognition into later periods.
3. Competition from larger battery or power solution vendors: Larger
players may have stronger balance sheets, better cell sourcing, or broader

customer relationships. If these competitors price aggressively,
Dynapack’s margins are likely to be under pressure.
4. Safety, certification and reliability risks: Any certification delay, field
failure, recall or reliability issue could damage Dynapack’s reputation,
resulting in share losses.
Our quantitative model assigns a High Risk rating to Dynapack. However, we
believe such a rating is not warranted for Dynapack due to: 1) the company is
generating solid revenue and earnings growth over next 3 years; the underlying

industry, BBU for AIDC, also enjoys secular growth; 2) the business model that
involves with product customization and strict safety/reliability requirements
would imply relatively benign competition and therefore stable pricing and
margins; and 3) the company has a strong balance sheet and has been in net cash
position since 2019.

Dynapack (3211.TWO): Company
Overview
Established in 1998 and listed on the Taipei Exchange in 2004, Dynapack is a
Taiwan-based lithium-ion battery pack manufacturer, focusing on customized
battery pack design, engineering, manufacturing and system integration.
Dynapack’s headquarters is located in Taoyuan, Taiwan with manufacturing
presence in Taiwan (A7 technology park), China, and Thailand.

Historically, Dynapack built its foundation in notebook and mobile-device battery
pack with certifications from major international brands including HP , ASUS,
Apple, Dell, and Microsoft. In recent years, the co has expanded beyond traditional
IT applications into higher-growth non-IT segments.
Dynapack assembles battery cells with protection circuits, mechanical parts,
software interfaces and related testing processes to meet customer’s system
requirement. Its key product categories include IT battery packs (for notebook,

tablet, mobile-devices), mobility and light EV battery packs (for e-bikes, e-
motors), BBU (for datacenter), energy storage and industrial applications (UPS,
ESS, AGV). In 2025, non-IT sales made up 35% of group sales, up from 5-10% in
2020. We estimate BBU to make up the majority of non-IT sales.

We think the competitive edge of Dynapack comes from its long operating history,
battery-pack design capability, international customer qualification, and
manufacturing flexibility. It holds international certifications including ISO 9001,
ISO 14001, IECQ QC080000, ISO 13485, ISO 17025, UL and TUV-related
certifications. Their capabilities allow the company to provide customized battery

pack solutions, while maintaining quality and reliability.
Real Estate Assets Provide Non-operating Earnings Support
Dynapack’s real estate assets have provided meaningful non-operating earnings
support in 2021 and 2024. The company owns land assets around Taoyuan’s A7
area and has monetized part of these asset through disposal and development
projects. In 2021, Dynapack sold its Guishan factory/office building and related
land, contributing c.NT$16/share to EPS. In 2024, the company recognized gains

from A7 land development and property disposal, contributing c.NT$12/share to
EPS. Going forward, the remaining A7 land could still provide additional asset value
or disposal gains.

Shareholder Structure
As of June 2026, Chairman Chung Tsung Ming is the largest shareholder, holding
c.7% of total shares. The overall founder and his family owns c.10% of total shares.
Local funds represented c.16% of shares while foreign investors made up 27% of
shares as of July 6th 2026.
Key Management Team
nChung Tsung Ming (Chairman) – Chairman Chung has a finance and accounting

background with an MBA from National Chengchi University and a bachelor’s
degree in accounting from the National Taiwan University. Prior to Dynapack, he
was a partner at Deloitte. He has served on Dynapack’s board since 2002.
nChang Chung Hsing (CEO) – President Chang was appointed in 2023. He holds a
master’s degree in electrical engineering from Chung Yuan University. Before
joining Dynapack, he worked as a senior manager of the power R&D center at

Dell.
nLin Yu Hui (CFO) – Ms. Lin serves as senior finance executive and the company’s
spokesperson. She holds a master’s degree in Accounting from National Taiwan
University. She was the manager of the audit department at Deloitte before
joining the firm.

Advanced Energy Solution (6781.TW)
Buy | TP NT$1,680.00 from NT$1,660.00 | Price NT$1,250.00 (06 Jul 26 13:30)
Reiterate Buy on strong AIDC BBU demand and HVDC migration — We remain 
constructive on AES as one of the beneficiaries of AIDC BBU adoption. BBU now 
contributes >70% of sales and should remain the key earnings driver as AI rack 
power continues to rise. We expect AES to benefit from higher BBU content per 
rack and deep CSP engagement as the industry transitions from conventional 48V 
systems to HVDC architecture. 
HVDC BBU mass production targeted from 2H26E through 1Q27E — We expect 
high-voltage (+/-400V and 800V) BBU solutions to enter volume production in 
early 2027, supported by next-generation AI racks with higher power density. The 
transition raises technical barriers which should favor established suppliers with 
proven system integration capability. While the market remains conservative on 
HVDC architecture progress, we see upside if commercialization progresses on 
schedule and BBU penetration continues to expand alongside AI rack deployment.   
Product diversifications outside of BBU; expanding capacity in China and 
Vietnam — In addition to BBU, we also see continued product diversifications into 
telecom, AGV/AMR and forklifting applications, although AIDC BBU should remain 
the dominant growth engine in the next 2- 3 years in our view. AES is accelerating 
capacity expansion in Vietnam and China to support the upcoming HVDC ramp. 
The company expects capex to increase 20-30% y/y in 2026E. As production 
scales, we expect stronger operating leverage and have more confidence in 
sustaining earnings growth in 2027E onwards. 
Earnings estimates and TP revision — We lower our earnings est 11%/7% in 
2026E/2027E to factor in higher opex assumptions, primarily driven by the 
ongoing investment in RD to support the upcoming HVDC ramp. Despite the 
earnings revisions, we raise our target price to NT$1,680 (from NT$1,660) as we roll 
forward our valuation base to 2027E EPS. We assign a 27x target P/E, on par with 
its historical average since listing. We use 2027E as the year of valuation base as 
we think 2027E can better reflect its earnings power following the 
commercialization of HVDC products.

Advanced Energy Solution
Company description
Established in January 2020 and listed in March 2021, Advanced Energy
Solution Holdings (AES) is a holding company registered in Cayman Island,
supplying battery packs for LEV (light electrical vehicle such as e-Bikes) and
BBU (battery back-up unit for datacenters) applications. Prior to the
establishment and IPO, AES was a BU focusing on non-IT applications within

its parent company, Simplo Technology (6121.TW).
Investment strategy
We rate AES shares as Buy. Being an industry leader in battery pack design
and manufacturing with a proven track record, we expect AES to benefit from
higher BBU content per rack and deep CSP engagement as the industry
transitions from conventional 48V systems to HVDC architecture. BBU now
contributes > 70% of sales and should remain the key earnings driver as AI
rack power continues to rise. We forecast earnings CAGR of 27% in 2025-

2028E, supported by strong BBU demand, mix upgrade toward high-power
BBU products and op leverage.
Valuation
Our target price of NT$1,680 is based on 27x 2026E EPS on par with its
historical average since listing and supported by a 2025-28E earnings CAGR
of 27%. We use 2027E as the year of valuation base as we think 2027E can
better reflect its earnings power after the commercializarion of HVDC
products.
Risks
Key downside risks to our earnings forecasts that could prevent the shares

from reaching our target price include: 1) slower-than-expected end demand
from e-Bikes post the pandemic and volaitlity in cloud capex deployment that
could impact datacenter BBU sales; 2) component supply
constraints/logistics challenges, which could lead to slower-than-expected
shipment and top-line momentum; and 3) peer competition, which could
impact sales growth and margins negatively, in our view.
Dynapack International
Company description

Established in 1998 and listed on the Taipei Exchange in 2004, Dynapack is a
Taiwan-based lithium-ion battery pack manufacturer, focusing on
customized battery pack design, engineering, manufacturing and system
integration. Dynapack built its foundation in notebook and mobile-device
battery packs with certifications from major international brands. In recent
years, it has expanded beyond traditional IT applications into higher-growth
non-IT segments. In 2025, non-IT sales made up 35% of group sales, up from

5-10% in 2020. We estimate BBU to make up the majority of non-IT sales.
Prepared for Kevin Lu

### Page 52

Taiwan Electronic Components & Equipment
07 July 2026 Citi Research
52
Investment strategy
We have a Buy rating on Dynapack shares. Our positive view is driven by
Dynapack's transition from a mature IT battery pack supplier to a key
beneficiary of AIDC BBU demand. As AI rack power density rises, we expect
BBU adoption and content value per rack to increase, supporting robust
revenue growth. We also expect meaningful margin expansion as product mix

shifts toward higher-margin BBU products. In addition, Dynapack's
partnership with multiple PSU operators should broaden its access to CSP
and AIDC customers. We forecast earnings CAGR of 60% in 2025-2028E.
Valuation
We assign a 32x target P/E to our 2027E EPS of NT$25 to derive a target price
of NT$800. We value Dynapack based on 2027E target P/E as we believe
2027E better reflects its earnings power after BBU capacity expansion. Our
target P/E of 32x is based on our forecast EPS CAGR of 66% in 2025-2027E

and a PEG of 0.5x, which we benchmark against its major PSU partner, as we
expect Dynapack to grow alongside its partner.
Risks
Our quantitative model assigns a High Risk rating to Dynapack. However, we
believe such a rating is not warranted for Dynapack due to: 1) the company is
generating solid revenue and earnings growth over next 3 years; the
underlying industry, BBU for AIDC, also enjoys secular growth; 2) the business
model that involves with product customization and strict safety/reliability

requirements would imply relatively benign competition and therefore stable
pricing and margins; and 3) the company has a strong balance sheet and has
been in net cash position since 2019.
Key downside risks to our price target/rating are: 1) Slower-than-expected
BBU adoption in AIDC, 2) Delay in PSU customer qualifications, 3)
Competition from larger battery or power solution vendors, 4) Safety,
certification and reliability issues.

Guide to Citi Research Fundamental Research Investment Ratings:
Citi Research stock recommendations include an investment rating and an optional risk rating to highlight high risk stocks.

Risk rating takes into account both price volatility and fundamental criteria. Stocks will either have no risk rating or a High risk
rating assigned.
Investment Ratings: Citi Research investment ratings are Buy, Neutral and Sell. Our ratings are a function of analyst
expectations of expected total return ("ETR") and risk. ETR is the sum of the forecast price appreciation (or depreciation) plus
the dividend yield for a stock within the next 12 months.  The target price is based on a 12 month time horizon. The Investment

rating definitions are: Buy (1) ETR of 15% or more or 25% or more for High risk stocks; and Sell (3) for negative ETR. Any covered
stock not assigned a Buy or a Sell is a Neutral (2). For stocks rated Neutral (2), if an analyst believes that there are insufficient
valuation drivers and/or investment catalysts to derive a positive or negative investment view, they may elect with the approval
of Citi Research management not to assign a target price and, thus, not derive an ETR. Citi Research may suspend its rating

and target price and assign “Rating Suspended” status for regulatory and/or internal policy reasons. Citi Research may also
suspend its rating and target price and assign "Under Review" status for other exceptional circumstances (e.g. lack of
information critical to the analyst's thesis, trading suspension) affecting the company and/or trading in the company's
securities. In both such situations, the rating and target price will show as “—“ and “-“ respectively in the rating history price

chart. Prior to 11 April 2022 Citi Research assigned “Under Review” status to both situations and prior to 11 Nov 2020 only in
exceptional circumstances. As soon as practically possible, the analyst will publish a note re-establishing a rating and
investment thesis. Investment ratings are determined by the ranges described above at the time of initiation of coverage, a
change in investment and/or risk rating, or a change in target price (subject to limited management discretion). At times, the

expected total returns may fall outside of these ranges because of market price movements and/or other short-term volatility
or trading patterns. Such interim deviations will be permitted but will become subject to review by Research Management.
Your decision to buy or sell a security should be based upon your personal investment objectives and should be made only
after evaluating the stock's expected performance and risk.

### Page 1

ASE Technology Holding

YTD investment tracking ahead of its ’26 
guide backed by solid AI CPU/ASIC demand

Reiterate Rating: BUY | PO: 750.00 TWD | Price: 679.00 TWD

YTD equipment buys tracks 66% of its ’26 capex guidance 
ASE has filed 82 equipment buys and 64 facility construction announcements through 
early July. While the filing may only capture the major payment, on the like for like basis, 
the spending on equipment has reached NT$175bn (Exhibit 1), booking 66% of its ’26 
capex guidance of US$8.5bn which is already revised up from the original US$7bn 
target. Specifically, the equipment mix is skewed toward 2.5D packaging (TSV, 
metrology, wet cleaning, flux coating, dispensing, molding, grinding, AOI and dicing) and 
testing (tester & prober). The limited space for further expansion also drove facility and 
clean room construction contracts to NT$82bn YTD mostly set to complete by 4Q28. 
Further capex upside for ‘26-27 as HPC gains accelerate 
We recently lifted our expectation for ASE capex in ‘26/27 to US$8.5bn/US$12.2bn (vs. 
US$5.5bn in ’25) in our CPU manufacturing report, close to TSMC’s back-end spending, 
on solid AI demand and foundry outsourcing. With YTD equipment buy tracking stronger, 
the company might need to further lift its capex to ~US$10bn in ’26 and US$13-15bn in 
’27, putting the capex/IC ATM sales elevated at 40% through ’28 (vs 10-yr avg. 20%) to 
fulfill its customers’ demand. While depreciation could ramp and funding would be 
required, the high utilization and better packaging/testing pricing should lift its IC ATM 
sales +34% CAGR from ’25-28 and expand GMs to 28%/33% in ‘26/27 on mix upgrade. 
Improving landscape and EPS upgrades support re-rating 
We keep our Buy rating on ASE with NT$750 PO on 20x 2H27-1H28 P/E and maintain 
EPS for ‘26/27/28 at NT$16/31/41. While the company may need to issue debt or equity 
in 2H26 to support its aggressive capex plan in 2027-28 for further 2.5D packaging and 
chip probing capacity expansion, it could secure the customer commitment while ROE 
from LEAP business at 25-30%+ should justify the cost of capital from the fundraising.

Company Sector 
Semiconductors

Company Description 
Established in 1984 and headquartered in Taiwan, ASE 
Technology Holding is the no.1 outsourced assembly and 
testing (OSAT) firm globally, in terms of market share by 
revenue. ASE acquired Siliconware Precision (SPIL) in 2018, 
and had acquired USI in 2010, which became its EMS 
business segment providing synergies in system-level 
packaging. 2 shares = 1 ADR.

Investment Rationale 
We rate ASE Buy, factoring in the company's opportunity in 
advanced packaging and testing evidenced in TSMC's 
outsourcing and its own heavy capex investment. The 
strategy shift should allow the company to capture fast 
growing addressable market in high performance 
computing applications and improves its margins. ASE 
could maintain its leading position in the Outsourced 
Semiconductor Assembly and Test (OSAT) universe, owing 
to its well-established footprints and widespread service 
offerings.

UBS Evidence Lab Global Data Centre Monitor
According to UBS Evidence Lab data, global operational capacity increased by 28GW in
2025 from 90GW in 2024, reaching a total of 118GW. This is higher than implied from
the 21GW capacity under construction at the end of 2024. North America/APAC/Europe

accounts for 45%/40%/14% of the total capacity, respectively.
Planned capacity increased significantly y/y, by 66GW or 88%, reaching 141GW by the
end of 2025. North America continues to dominate, accounting for 65% of the planned
capacity  while APAC and Europe are both at 16-17%. Under construction capacity is at
34GW globally by end of 2025. We see this as a good indicator of the capacity addition
within a 1-year time frame, and see upside from this based on the evidence from

2024/25.  In Q1 2026, operational capacity increased by another 6GW while planned
capacity saw a significant growth of 20GW.

 Expert call on 800VDC  ( link). 800V DC architecture is emerging as the next
standard in data centres, driven by rising rack density, with adoption still early but

expected to accelerate. It delivers c.1–3% efficiency gains per conversion, with
potential total power savings of ~5%, alongside lower system costs, reduced
copper usage and simplified infrastructure (less need for UPS, inverters and PDUs).
While insulation and EMI challenges remain, the shift will favour high-voltage
technology players and reduce demand for traditional low-voltage components.

### Page 6

Data Centre Central UBS Research
800VDC Architecture 101
800V DC is emerging as a structural shift in data centre power architecture, driven by
rapidly rising rack densities that are pushing traditional low-voltage AC systems to their
limits. By increasing voltage, operators can reduce current for a given power level, which
lowers copper usage, reduces heat losses and improves efficiency—effectively enabling
continued scaling toward several hundred kW and ultimately MW-class racks.

Architecturally, this implies a move from distributing low-voltage AC across the facility to
rectifying power earlier and distributing high-voltage DC, with conversion happening
closer to the chip. This reduces the role of low-voltage AC switchgear and PDUs, while
increasing the importance of DC distribution, protection and power electronics.
Medium-voltage infrastructure remains in place, and UPS evolves rather than
disappears, shifting toward lithium-ion and more distributed configurations.

Adoption is expected to be phased. Near-term solutions (e.g. sidecar or centralized DC
architectures) focus on supporting higher rack density while leveraging existing supply
chains. Over time, the industry is likely to move toward more fully DC-based systems
incorporating solid-state transformers and advanced DC-DC conversion. However,
multiple architectures are likely to coexist for an extended period, suggesting a gradual
transition rather than a rapid, standardised shift. The efficiency benefits are meaningful

but incremental, with savings driven by fewer conversion steps and lower copper
intensity, partially offset by greater spend on DC switchgear, controls and protection.
The transition also introduces new technical challenges, including insulation, safety and
EMI management, increasing system complexity.
From a vendor perspective, the shift primarily drives a mix change. Exposure to high-
voltage systems, DC distribution and advanced power electronics becomes increasingly

valuable, favouring players with strong capabilities in these areas. Conversely, pure low-
voltage AC exposure faces structural pressure unless offerings are expanded up the
voltage stack. Overall, 800V DC represents an evolution of the electrical architecture,
redistributing value toward higher-voltage, more integrated and more software-enabled
solutions rather than reducing total addressable spend.
Figure 10: Data Centre architecture available today

Source: Company reports, UBS estimates.

### Page 7

Figure 11: Three phases of 800V DC architecture
Source: Company reports, UBS estimates. *Icon represents 800V DC sidecar power distribution unit.
Today's data centre power architecture is fundamentally an AC distribution system.
Power enters the facility at medium voltage, is stepped down through transformers to LV
AC, passes through UPS systems, and is distributed around the data hall via AC busbars
before finally reaching rack PDUs. Conversion to the DC voltages required by chips

ultimately occurs inside server power supplies.
The architecture is well proven and highly resilient, but it requires multiple conversion
stages and significant quantities of LV electrical equipment. As rack densities increase
beyond traditional enterprise and cloud workloads, the efficiency and physical footprint
of this power chain become increasingly important design constraints
Figure 12: Current data centre architecture (version 1)
Source: UBS

### Page 8

A second common architecture inserts additional distribution layers, including central
PDUs and remote power panels, between the UPS and IT equipment. This approach
improves operational flexibility and allows operators to support larger deployments, but
adds further equipment, floor space and electrical conversion stages.
Figure 13: Current data centre architecture (version 2)
Source: UBS
Phase 1 represents the first meaningful shift away from traditional AC distribution.

While the upstream architecture remains largely intact, an AC-to-DC power shelf is
introduced before the rack line-up, creating an 800V DC distribution bus that feeds the
racks directly.
The key change is that power conversion moves closer to the facility level rather than
occurring repeatedly inside individual servers. Rack-level equipment receives 800V DC
and converts it to 48V or 12V DC for IT hardware. This reduces conversion losses,
simplifies server power architectures and helps support rack densities of c.150kW,

materially above most current deployments.
From a supplier perspective, the value pool begins to migrate away from conventional
rack PDUs towards high-power rectifiers, DC conversion systems and rack-level DC-DC
power electronics. However, we see the disruption to incumbent electrical vendors as
relatively limited given it does not remove a significant part of the existing installed base.
This makes ORV3 an attractive near-term migration path for operators seeking higher

rack densities without redesigning the entire facility power chain.

### Page 9

Figure 14: Phase 1 (ORV3) - introduction of 800V DC
Source: UBS
Figure 15: Evolution of current architecture to Phase 1
Source: UBS
Phase 2 introduces the sidecar architecture which pushes power conversion even closer
to the rack. Rather than distributing AC through busbars and multiple downstream
distribution devices, a dedicated sidecar power cabinet converts 400V AC directly into
Phase 1 adds an 800V DC layer to the
existing architecture, centralising

power conversion and enabling
higher rack densities with minimal
disruption to existing infrastructure

### Page 10

800V DC adjacent to the rack row.
Centralising conversion within the sidecar reduces the amount of power equipment
located within the rack itself, freeing up valuable compute space. The architecture is
designed to support rack densities approaching 400kW.
The sidecar model removes a larger portion of the traditional AC distribution stack.
Functions previously performed by busbars, rack PDUs and associated rack-level AC
infrastructure are consolidated into a dedicated sidecar conversion cabinet positioned

adjacent to the compute racks.
For electrical equipment suppliers, this phase represents a more meaningful architectural
transition than ORV3 because existing product categories begin to be substituted.
Figure 16: Phase 2 (sidecar architecture)
Source: UBS

### Page 11

Figure 17: Evolution of current architecture to sidecar
Source: UBS
Phase 3 removes the largest proportion of today's electrical infrastructure. Conventional
transformers, low-voltage switchboards, low-voltage UPS systems and much of the AC
distribution chain are replaced by medium-voltage UPS systems, solid-state transformers
and native DC distribution.
In this architecture, power is converted from 11kV AC directly into 800V DC, eliminating
several intermediate stages. Short-duration energy storage stabilises the DC bus and

supports the highly dynamic power requirements of future AI clusters. The facility
evolves from an AC distribution network into a predominantly DC power system.
If commercialised at scale, a full solid-state architecture could support rack densities
approaching 1MW while materially reducing conversion losses, equipment count and
electrical footprint.

Key Newsflow and research
 Learnings from Q2 previews
 Legrand mentioned they have a sidecar prototype which we think they will fully
launch at the CMD in September. They continue to see a neutral to positive
impact for 80% of sales, with a negative impact for 20% of its sales. They
expect hybrid (with sidecar) to begin generating sales in 2027/8 with the
market growing to 10-20% of all new IT loads in 2030.
 Schneider is now seeing the price impact in P&L in Q2. The message for H1

Gross Margin remained 'flat to slightly down', which we now view as closer to
flat than down. Regarding Data Centres, we expect strong dynamics to
continue.
 ABB mentioned Data Centre demand continues to stand out. They already
have DC breaker based on power electronics and semiconductor and also
rectifier in its Motion business. ABB are also developing an SST product and
does not plan on doing the sidecar since it believes it sits in a transitory

category. Additionally, ABB believe the MV UPS will be a very important
product category as it moves UPS from smaller scale to a more system level
power supply.
 Siemens saw Electrification and Data Centre growing strongly. We believe that
Data Centre demand will remain at elevated levels for a few years. We forecast
30% organic order growth in Q3'26.
 Expert session on European data center market outlook ( link). The European
data centre market continues to benefit from strong demand, with AI expected to

become the primary growth driver as AI workloads increase to 3.5x 2025 levels by
2030 and account for 71% of total demand (vs. 54% today). However, power
availability rather than demand is increasingly the main constraint, particularly in
FLAP-D markets, supporting growth in secondary markets such as Iberia. Despite a
temporary slowdown in hyperscaler spending during 2025, activity has
reaccelerated in 2026. The sector is also attracting a broader investor base as data

centres evolve into a hybrid real estate-infrastructure asset class, with permitting,
grid access and delivery certainty remaining more important drivers of returns than
construction cost inflation.
 Meta  makes cloud push to sell excess AI compute power capacity
(link).Meta is considering either selling "raw" compute capacity to external
companies or access to various AI models that are hosted on Meta’s existing
infrastructure. UBS Internet Services analyst flag that CEO Mark Zuckerberg had

previously floated both of these options on various public calls and as such this is
not new news.  As this new line of business was not part of what Mr. Zuckerberg
had previously articulated as long term opportunities, some investors may be wary
of a pivot. They think that either of these developments will plug some of the
duration problem that has ailed the stock, as selling cloud capacity or model access
will theoretically yield higher near-term revenue versus waiting for Meta Business

Agents and Meta AI chatbots to scale.
 Google unveils new open-source liquid-to-air cooling sidecar for air-cooled
environments (link). Google has introduced “Brazos,” an open-source, rack-
mounted, closed-loop liquid-to-air cooling sidecar designed to enable incremental
deployment of high-density liquid cooling within existing air-cooled data centers.
The system captures heat at the component level using liquid cooling and
dissipates it into the hot aisle via integrated heat exchangers, offering liquid-

cooling performance with air-cooling operational simplicity. Brazos is modular
(three units per rack, ~60kW total load), compatible with standard OCP ORv3
racks, and supports deionized water or glycol mixtures while operating on 40–60V
DC via rack busbars. It incorporates safety and management features such as leak
detection, pressure relief, and remote monitoring, and is already commercially
ready via partners. By open-sourcing its design, Google aims to accelerate industry

adoption of scalable cooling solutions for AI-driven high-power workloads,
extending broader Open Compute Project efforts alongside similar sidecar
approaches from Microsoft, Meta, and AWS. Our take:   We note that 60kW is
clearly above traditional compute at 20-30kW but well below the "AI grade" of
100kW+. We don’t think this represents a threat to data centre cooling companies
and would see it as  a rather generic solution trying to make higher densities work

### Page 14

without a full liquid to chip setup.
 Data4 confirms €5bn plan for 700MW AI data center in northern France
(link). Data4 has confirmed plans to develop a €5bn, 700MW AI-focused data
center campus in Escaudain, northern France, marking its largest project to date
and one of Europe’s largest single-site digital infrastructure investments.  The
project benefits from strong government backing, fast-track grid access, and a
strategically attractive location within a key European connectivity corridor, and

forms part of France’s broader ambition to position itself as a leading AI
infrastructure hub. Our take: Our colleagues in Transportation/Construction team
also recently noted an acceleration in planned Data centre projects in Europe/
France - they see it as   a potential tailwind mid-term. Earlier in the year, our
Sustainability team wrote about France entering a phase of structural overcapacity
in low-carbon electricity. In their opinion, France has spare, clean and reliable

power at scale, and with more stable marginal costs than fossil-linked systems, at a
time when demand from AI, data centres, industry and broader electrification is
accelerating.
 Alderbuck Energy to deploy solid-state transformer at San Diego
Supercomputer Center (link). The company will deploy its Nexus Power Unit,
which is a medium-voltage solid-state transformer that consolidates multiple
pieces of conventional grid equipment into a single modular system. This, the

company claims, cuts project capital costs by 20-30 percent, reduces physical
footprint by a similar margin, shortens construction timelines by 30-50 percent,
and offers up to four percent higher energy efficiency. The project will assess a
12kV AC-to-800VDC configuration against conventional 480V AC systems,
generating operational data on powering high-density AI workloads. Prior to
deployment, the unit will undergo testing and simulation at UC San Diego’s

DERConnect facility.
 South Korea announces US$500bn chip investment on huge AI demand
(link). South Korea has announced a record KRW 800 trillion (US$518bn)
investment to expand its semiconductor industry, driven by surging demand from
AI data centres, with plans to build four new memory fabrication plants in the
southwest to establish a second major production hub outside Seoul. Backed by
major industry players including Samsung and SK Hynix, the initiative  represents

one of the largest corporate investment commitments in the country to date.

Valuation Method and Risk Statement
The engineering sector is cyclical by nature. Our estimates and the share prices are therefore
likely to be sensitive to changes in expectations for global or regional growth and industrial
activity. Exchange rate fluctuations contribute additional risk to the sector. We value the
stocks in our engineering coverage universe based on the average of cash flow (DCF, residual
income and DDM) and static (multiple-based) valuation methodologies.

Industry View In-Line
We continue to forecast 70-80K racks in CY26: This year should remain a strong
one for downstream rack assembly. We expect over 100% y/y growth in rack

shipments, vs. ~29k last year.
Quanta (2382.TW, OW): June revenue was NT$385.2B (+24% m/m, +103% y/y). We
attribute the m/m growth primarily to higher GB200/300 rack shipments in the
month, while NB shipments were also higher m/m at 4.5M units.  But for
GB200/300 rack shipments in the month, we estimate Quanta shipped 2.3-2.4K,
higher than the 1.8-1.9K racks shipped in May. This brings overall 2Q GB200/300
rack shipments to approximately 6.2-6.3K (+32% q/q), slightly below our prior

forecast of ~6.7K units, with the lowered rack shipments likely just pushed out into
2H. Our full-year assumption is unchanged at ~18.7K racks.
Wistron (3231.TW, OW): June revenue was  NT$321.8B (+11% m/m, +54% y/y). We
attribute the m/m growth to 1) higher revenue from Wiwynn (revenue grew 33% m/
m, to NT$111.4B), 2) higher monitor shipments at 1,000K units (+5% m/m), 3) higher
DT shipments at 800K units (+33% m/m), and 4) higher NB shipments at 2M units

(+18% m/m), offset slightly by lower GB200/300 server computing tray shipments
(1,200-1,300 rack equivalents, by our estimates, down 5-10% m/m). This brings
overall 2Q rack shipments to 3.9-4.0K units (flattish q/q), slightly below our prior
forecast of ~4.2K, with the lowered rack shipments likely just pushed out into 2H.
Our full-year assumption is unchanged at ~14.1K racks.
Hon Hai (2317.TW, OW): June revenue was NT$821.8B (-4% m/m, +52% y/y), with 1)

the consumer segment, which mainly includes iPhone assembly, seeing slowing pull-
ins and declining slightly m/m, 2) server-related revenue seeing sustained
momentum for AI products, coming in flattish m/m, and 3) the computing segment
falling slightly m/m. We model HH's GB rack shipments as flattish m/m at ~3.3K
units, resulting in overall 2Q rack shipments of ~10.3K units (+21% q/q), slightly
above our prior forecast of ~10K. For 3Q, it expects AI-related rack shipments to

communications with a subject company, public appearances
and trading securities held by a research analyst account.
Key Takeaways
We estimate GB200/300 rack output in June at ~8.0K (+5% m/m), within which:
Quanta shipped 2.3-2.4K  GB200/GB300 racks.
Wistron shipped 1.2-1.3K GB200/GB300 racks.
Hon Hai shipped ~3.3K GB200/300 racks.

Hon Hai Precision (2317.TW)
Base case scenario value, derived from a residual income valuation model. Our key assump-
tions include a cost of equity of 8.5%, a medium-term growth rate of 13%, and a terminal
growth rate of 3%.
Risks to Upside
n Better-than-expected iPhone sell-through
n Faster progress in AI server business
n Faster EV business development progress
n Any new M&A activity that could improve sentiment

Risks to Downside
n Lower iPhone sell-through
n Smaller profit contribution from AI business
n Slower EV business development progress
n Geopolitical developments that could negatively affect foreign investment
Quanta Computer Inc. (2382.TW)
Base case, residual income model. Key assumptions include a cost of equity of 9.0% (beta of
1.2, equity premium of 6.0% and risk-free rate of 1.5%), an 8.5% medium-term growth rate, and
a 3% terminal growth rate.

Risks to Upside
n Stronger-than-expected NB demand
n Stronger-than-expected Apple Watch demand
n Stronger-than-expected server demand
n Faster-than-expected AI server penetration
Risks to Downside
n Weaker-than-expected NB demand
n Softer-than-expected Apple Watch demand
n Weak margin performance owing to rising labor costs and sales shortfalls
n Fierce price competition in the mega data center segment

2Q26/3Q26 EPS 估 2.5/2.8 元，下修主因維修毛利率低於預期 
2Q26/3Q26 營收估 50.7/53.3 億元，季增 7%/5%，皆維持前次預估。毛利率
估 26.4%/26.7%，季減 1.1/季增 0.3 個 ppts，皆下修 1.3 個 ppts，估主因維
修品項較 1Q26 簡易，維修毛利率略低於預期；營益率估 22.8%/23.1%，季
減 1.0 個 ppts/季增 0.4 個 ppts，皆下修 1.3 個 ppts。2Q26/3Q26 EPS 2.5/2.8
元，季減 1%/季增 8%，下修 6%/5%。子公司長異 2Q26 營收受供應鏈缺料
影響，估整體營運損平；整體 2Q/3Q26 維修業務隨飛 機機齡與保有輛持續
提升、製造業務隨交機提升，同步穩定成長。 
無人機法案朝野共識漸趨明朗，供應鏈重啟再即 
本中心預估 2026/27 年長榮航太營收年增 15%/23%至 208 億元/256 億元，
持平/上修 7%。2027 年上修主因無人機專案隨近期朝野協商共識漸趨一致，
預期 2026/07/03 將商討朝野各黨團提出無人機採購方式、流程與相關配套措
施。儘管各黨團對預算來源、在地採購與自製率與相關有所不同，然各黨團
皆支持無人機在地化發展、帶動台灣供應鏈與在地化目標趨於一致。 估無人
載具預算至遲有望於 2027 年正式落地。本中心維持上修 2027/28/年無人機
業務營收預估至 20/50 億元(營收占比 8%/16%，較前次 5 億元/-有所上修)。 
維修價量齊揚及 2027 年機體製造業務與無人機挹注成長 
公司受惠三大動能：1) 漲價與維修量雙增，帶動營運槓桿發酵。2) 長異維修
業務隨 GE 擴大全球 MRO 量能重返成長。 3) 空巴機體與無人機業務 挹注
2027 年獲利成長。估 2027/28 年無人機營收達 20 億元/50 億元，營收占比
8%/16%。2026/27/28 年 EPS 估年增 87%/21%/17%至 10.2/12.4/14.5 元，
下修 4%/上修 3%/-。上修 2027 年 EPS 主因看好無人機預算與供應鏈重啟機
率高。以 22 倍本益比及 2026-2027 年平均 EPS(前次 20 倍，上修 2 倍主因
看好無人機業務於 2027 年貢獻)，得目標價 250 元，給予買進評等。 
元大觀點 
⧫

1Q26 簡易，維修毛利率略低於預期。業外長異子公司估損平。 
⧫  
無人 機預算估至遲有望於 2027 年正式落地，本中心上修長榮航太
2027/28 年無人機業務營收預估至 20/50 億元(營收占比 8%/16%) 。 
⧫  
受惠維修價量齊揚、長異營運回升及 2027 年無人機與製造業務挹注。
以 22 倍本益比，2026-27 年平均 EPS 得目標價 250 元，買進評等。

題，營運槓桿將持續發酵。帶動 2026/27 年營益率估達 21.8%/21.5%，年增 5.3 個 ppts/年減 0.3 個
ppts。2027 年營益率年減主因低毛利製造業務占比提升及觀音新廠開出。2)、長異發動機業務持續
復甦且自 4Q25 已連續兩季度盈利。顯示 GE 引擎維修需求顯著提升。後續隨 GE 引擎保有量提升、
擴大 MRO 業務與外包+營運賠償損失影響低於預期下，將成長強勁。3)、2027 年觀音新廠擴產開
出，支持空巴、波音機體零組件訂單與軍用商規無人機訂單 。 
本中心預估 2026/27 年長榮航太營收年增 15%/23%至 208 億元/256 億元，持平/上修 7%。2027 年
上修主因無人機專案隨近期朝野協商共識漸趨一致，預期 2026/07/03 將商討朝野各黨團提出無人
機採購方式、流程與相關配套措施。儘管各黨團對預算來源、在地採購與自製率與相關有所不同，
然各黨團支持無人機在地化發展、帶動台灣供應鏈與在地化目標趨於一致。本中心認為無人載具預
算至遲有望於 2027 年正式落地，帶動台灣供應鏈需求提升。本中心維持 2026 年長榮航太無人機尚
未有營收貢獻；上修 2027/28 年無人機業務營收預估至 20/50 億元(營收占比 8%/16%，較前次 5 億
元/-有所上修)。2026/27 年毛利率下修 0.7/0.9 個 ppts 至 25.5%/25.1%，年增 5.1 個 ppts/年減 0.4
個 ppts。營益率下修 0.7/0.9 個 ppts 至 21.8%/21.5%，年增 5.3 個 ppts/年減 0.2 個 ppts。估 2026/27
年 EPS 年增 87%/21%至 10.2/12.4 元，下修 4%/上修 3%。上修 2027 年 EPS 主因加入無人機業務

產業概況  
機隊維修為疫後新商機，供不應求狀況持續 
根據 Oliver Wyman 預測，全球商用機隊數量將從 2025 年的 28,400 架 成長至 2035 年的 36,400 
架，其中平均機齡已接近  12 年，反映出大量機體與引擎將進入維修高峰期。 2025 年新交機量達 
1,750 架，但受限於供應鏈瓶頸，產能仍無法全面滿足航空公司需求，迫使業者延長老舊機服役年
限。整體商用航空 MRO 市場規模預估將從 2030 年的 1,330 億美元成長至 2035 年的 1,560 億美
元，其中引擎維修（Engine MRO ）仍為最大子領域，佔整體約  43%，年均成長率約 2.3%。同時，
勞動力缺口日益擴大，預估 2035 年前全球將短缺超過 90,000 名航空維修技師，特別在北美與歐洲
最為嚴重，進一步推升維修價格與外包需求。 
圖 14：MRO 市場穩定成長

資料來源：Oliver Wyman 
國防策略偏重無人機，長榮航太為中、大型主要供應商 
2024 年在民進黨延續執政下，五大產業方針之一的國防產業 -無人機成為顯學。政策目標將台灣打
造成亞太區無人機生產重鎮，預計至 2028 年無人機產值成長 10 倍達 300 億元，無人機月產能
15,000 架次，利用內需市場與補強技術缺口等方式，打造無人機供應鏈。 
根據 2025 年台灣國防預算細項來看，國防無人載具預算占總國防預算 3.1%/203 億元，其中一半以
上用於採購美國 MQ-9B 高空無人機系統。本中心認為，台灣國防於中大型軍用軍規無人機將以美
國採購為主，輔以本土自製大 型無人機。然其餘中、低階軍用商規無人機將發包並利用民間量能。
目前台灣第一波軍用商規無人機將於未來四年採購 3,600 架，共 69.5 億元預算。第二波預期將採購
近 4.9 萬架次，總預算估達 725 億元，目標於 2027 年前建置完畢。2027 年後航太小組估計仍將為
全國基礎建設等重要設施加購無人機達 5 萬架次，輔以俄烏戰爭烏克蘭每月消耗超過萬台 FPV 無人
機來看，本中心預估台灣軍用無人機市場產值將以 CAGR 96%自 2024 年 19.5 億元成長到 2030 年
1,100 億元。

請參閱末頁之免責宣言。 台灣：航太與國防 2026 年 7 月 2 日 Evergreen Aviation

後疫情時代跨境隨需求復甦、缺工、缺料緩解，新訂單需求持續挹注下，供應鏈將
於逐步重返疫情前水準 
綜觀全球航太市場屬寡佔市場。飛機製造大廠以空巴、波音為主，市佔率接近 80%。又整體供應鏈
認證期長，主因航太產業中的各項零組件及引擎與國防相關產品如戰鬥機可共用零組件，因此不僅
是終端產品需經過原廠認證，製造期間的原物料、板金成形、特殊表面處理等多須經過由美國航太
和國防工業巨頭與美國國防部、SAE 等機構共同發起的 NADCAP-國際航太和國防工業供應商認證
體系的認證，因此一旦打入航太產業供應鏈，除非出現重大瑕疵品，否則供應商不容易產生巨大變
化。 
2020 年受到新冠疫情影響，全球航空客運量需求自疫情前高點下滑超過 80%。在疫情衝擊下，全
球航空旅行活動大幅減少，波音、空中巴士、奇異、勞斯 萊斯等航太大廠面對新機需求銳減，紛紛
減產、裁員、降低外包。然隨疫情逐漸流感化及疫苗接種率逐步攀升下，於 1H23 全球航空客運量
已復甦至 2019 年疫情前的 94.2%。而如今當跨國流動需求大幅提升時，供應鏈生產出現二大問題，
包含 1) 疫情期間大量裁員或提前退休造成缺工現象； 2) 小型零組件廠倒、運輸問題、原物料廠商
缺工都造成長短料現象，使引擎及整機出現供不應求狀況。同時間，因為復飛成本 (包含零組件檢
查、維修、舊機種燃油耗損大及新機種碳排量低於舊機種約 25-40%等因素)大於新購機種情況下將
推升新機採購需求。以 2024 年波音與空巴年交付量共 1,114 架，積壓訂單 15,461 架次來看，至少
須 11 年才能消化完畢。由於飛機交機時程持續拉長，航空公司在疫情後紛紛提早下單滿足未來航
運需求，從波音與空巴訂單數量來看，亦可見自 1Q21 以來淨訂單便自谷底的 2 架次持續復甦到近
期 4Q25 的 650 架次，積壓訂單持續增加使整體航太產業需求無虞。

航太供應鏈毛利率持續壓縮，轉型核心零組件、維修及位階升級朝 Tier 1 邁進 
國際航太飛機及發動機製造供應鏈為垂直分工，分為以下階層：元件 /生料供應商(Tier 4) 、零組件
供應商(Tier 3)、次系統供應商(Tier 2) (機載設備、模組段特殊零件)及主體結構主要組件供應商(Tier 
1)，最上層則為機體結構全機整合和飛機引擎整機製造等原廠(OEM)。 
目前歐美主要飛機及引擎製造公司均採全球分工方式，建立零組件供應鏈體系。國際航太大廠持續
要求降價，以及新興國家在政府的支持下以低生產成本切入單一化零件加工 。而台灣目前多位於供
應鏈 Tier 2 及以下，廠商包含漢翔、駐龍、晟田、長榮航太等，生產產品又以機匣、起落架及結構
零組件等非核心零組件為主。主因發動機核心鍛造件需大量資本支出與時間去研發，也使得台灣航
太供應鏈廠商降價壓力與日俱增。台廠在基礎航太零組件毛利逐漸承壓下，未來將逐漸發展較為精
密的熱鍛組合件或是高毛利的民用發動機 MRO ( 維護、維修與整修)，期待能打造一站式解決方案，
提供包含發動機內部高精度鑄造件、組合件、系統件、機體結構、起落架以及後續維運服務，以提
升在整體航太產業鏈的產值。

獲利調整與股票評價  
維修與製造本業需求強勁，無人機專案在朝野黨團目標一致下，2027 年有望落地 
長榮航太受惠三大成長動能，包含 1) 疫後空運需求持續成長且飛機保有量持續提升下，帶動整體
MRO 維修需求。公司透過漲價/招工方式提升產能，帶動維修業務營收成長。2) 長異發動機維修隨
GE 擴大全球 MRO 量能重返成長。3) 空巴機體業務挹注 2027 年營收/獲利成長。近期隨無人機預
算編列，各黨團立場趨於一致下，估無人機產業鏈 2027 年有望落使交付，帶動 2026/27/28 年 EPS
估年增 87%/21%/17%至 10.2/12.4/14.5 元。上修 2027 年 EPS 3%，主因無人機業務預算與供應鏈
重啟機率高，上修 2027 年無人機營收自 5 億元提升至 20 億元，營收占比 8%；2028 年無人機營收
達 50 億元，營收占比 16%。 
本中心預估長榮航太 2026/27/28 年 EPS 年增 87%/21%/17%至 10.2/12.4/14.5 元，下修 4%/上修
3%/-，受惠 2027 年無人機業務挹注成長。公司近三年平均預期本益比達 20 倍，近期公司營運將進
入快速成長期，透過漲價 /招工人因應維修產能不足，同時打開空巴機體零組件市場，成長動能無
虞；加以近期無人載具預算在朝野黨團目標漸趨一致下，有望於 2027 年始落地，上調本益比至 22
倍(前次 20 倍)，以 2026-2027 年平均 EPS 11.3 元，得目標價 250 元，給予買進評等。

公司簡介  
長榮航太 80%營收來自機隊維護、維修與營運 (MRO-Maintenance /Repairment/Overhaul) 業務，其中長榮航空占其總營收
約 30%，大多來自其機隊維修，其他包含全日空、韓亞航空、天馬航空…，另外亦包含貨運機隊 UPS 維修等等。公司維修
業務 60%為機體維修，其他包含線上維修、零件維修、引擎維修等等。製造業務佔營收比重約 20%，主要以引擎零組件如
引擎燃燒筒匣、發動機擴散器、燃燒室內/外支撐架等為主，引擎零組件占其中 80%，主要維修 GE 引擎。另外 20%為波音
機體零組件，主要包含貨機防撞牆、艙門等等。此外，長榮航太擁有三家子公司  : 包涵與 GE 合資的長翼股份有限公司，主
要執行 GE 引擎 MRO 業務。長鋭航材為與 Spirit Aerospace 合資公司，發展機體維修業務。長鑽科技則主要負責表面處理
與化學處理等業務。主要損益來源以長翼股份有限公司為主。

ESG 分析  
分別藉由「在 ESG 議題上的曝險」和「個別公司在 ESG 議題上的執行力」兩個面向來衡量公司於 ESG 上的表現。 
► ESG 總分： 長榮航太整體的 ESG 風險評級屬於低風險，於 Sustainalytics 資料庫所覆蓋的公司中排名亦排行於領先的
位置，在航空行業的公司中排名也領先同業。 
► 在 ESG 議題上的曝險： 長榮航太的整體曝險屬於低風險，但仍略優於航空行業的平均水準。公司較需要改善的 ESG 
議題包含人力資源、公司數據安全、商業道德等。 
► 個別公司在 ESG 議題上的執行力：長榮航太在針對重大 ESG 議題的管理水準和執行力屬高等。公司遵循適當的 ESG 
揭露，表明對投資者和公眾的強烈責任感。其 ESG 相關問題由董事會或經營團隊負責，建議將這些整合到核心業務戰
略中。

報告日期： 2026/07/01 研 究 員：洪  瑞 陽(Ryan Hung) 
壹、投 資 建 議

一、 1Q26 營收 3.52 億元，稅後 EPS 1.39 元 
璟德  1Q26 營收  3.52 億元， QoQ +2.0% 、YoY −8.8% ，毛利率  
45.1% 、營業利益率  28.9% ，稅後淨利  0.96 億元、稅後  EPS 1.39 
元(以減資前股本 6.9 億元計算 )。單季營收仍處相對低檔，主因第
一季為傳統淡季，且公司主動淡化大陸手機之削價競爭、擇優安
排產能所致 ； 惟毛利率受惠寬頻新應用占比提升而維持 45% 較高
水準，反映產品組合持續優化。展望後續，公司月營收已於 2026
年 4 月起轉為年增、 5 月達 1.36 億元 YoY +17.6% ，擺脫 2025 年
3 月以來連續  13 個月的年減，顯示營運已自谷底回升， 1Q26 可
望為今年營收低點。

二、預 估2Q26 營收 4.06 億元 ， QoQ +15.3% ，YoY+14%  
預估璟德 2Q26 營收 4.06 億元， QoQ +15.3% ，YoY +14% ，1H26 
營收  7.58 億元， YoY +2.1% ，營收谷底回升。觀察月營收自 2025
年 3 月起長達 13 個月的年減首次在 2026 年 4 月 轉 正，自1.1 億左
右的谷底回升至 1.2-1.3 億以上的水準 。2Q26 毛利率  44.3% ，QoQ 
−0.8 ppts ，主因原物料成本上漲；營業利益率  29.8% ，QoQ +0.9 
ppts ；稅後淨利率  25% ，QoQ −2.2 ppts ，主因處分廠房之資本利
得稅及匯損，預估單季稅後  EPS 1.47 元， 1H26 累計稅後  EPS 
2.86 元(減資前股本 )。營收結構方面，預估 2Q26 寬頻新應用占  
58% 、WiFi 占 33% 、手機占  9% ，相較  1H25 之 40% ／41% ／
19% 大幅轉向高毛利寬頻新應用；以絕對金額計， 1H26 寬頻新
應用營收  4.32 億元 、YoY +45.5% ，WiFi 2.50 億元 、YoY −18.0%，
手機  0.76 億元、 YoY −46.1% 。

三、寬頻新應用為成長主軸，持續優化產品組合  
1H26 寬頻新應用占營收 58%、WiFi 33% 、手機  9% ，相較  1H25 
之 40% ／41% ／19% ，營運重心已大幅轉向寬頻新應用。其中，
手機業務因大陸市場價格競爭激烈，擇優安排產能使占比降至
9%；WiFi 則為營運基本盤 ， 未來有望受惠於 WiFi 7 與 AI PC 需
求帶動。此次獲利結構優化的主因在於寬頻領域的「高單價」與
「高客戶黏著度」 。璟德提供能解決高頻雜訊的「整合型射頻解決
方案」。在寬頻應用領域 (如：低軌衛星、車載感測、國防、智慧
城市等 ) ，此類客製化模組具備極高的排他性，一旦獲客戶  
Design-in 即極難被替換。預估使其寬頻產品單顆  ASP 高達一般

合評價與產業趨勢，給予區間操作之投資建議，建議於 289~356
元(26x~32x 2027EPS) 之間區間操作。

一家專注於高頻整合元件與模組的設計及製造公司，主要透過低
溫陶瓷 (LTCC) 技術研發製造無線通訊元件與模組，公司低溫陶瓷

客戶決定電路要做什麼 (系統 /規格層 )；璟德決定這個電路怎麼用  
LTCC 立體實現成一顆模組 (元件 /模組設計＋製造層 )。它不是只
照規格量產標準被動元件，而是能自行設計元件結構、把  Balun 、
耦合器、 LPF ＋switch(ASM) 等功能整合成  3D 模組並製造，因而
能依客戶需求變化、且  Design-in 後難以替換。

二、營運概況及展望

1.產業重心轉向「寬頻新應用」 ，配合減資迎來新氣象  
營運重心轉向高單價寬頻新應用。 1H26 寬頻新應用占營收  
57% 、WiFi 33% 、手機  10% ，相較  1H25 之 40% ／41% ／19% ，
營運重心已大幅轉向寬頻。其中手機業務因大陸市場價格競爭激
烈、公司擇優安排產能，占比降至個位數； WiFi 為營運基礎，台
灣市場價格相對穩定，中長期可望受惠  WiFi 7 與 AI PC 換機需
求。寬頻新應用涵蓋低軌衛星、車載感測、國防、智慧城市與智
慧抄表等，係此次獲利結構優化之核心；此類客製化模組排他性
高、Design-in 後黏著度極強、單價遠高於一般品，公司表示國防
相關、車載感測器用量增加，為寬頻成長主要動能。  
區域結構同步轉向歐美高階市場。北美市場營收占比由  2024 年
約 30.7% 、2025 年約  35.8% ，提升至  1H26 之 52% ；亞洲 (主要
為中國 )則由  2024 年約  47.5% 逐年收斂至  1H26 之 29% ；台 灣
內銷穩定於  19~21% 。公司逐步捨棄殺價競爭且波動劇烈之中國
市場 ， 轉向認證期較長(約 6~12 個月 )但單價高 、 訂單黏著之北美
市場；其與兩大美系客戶之合作已逾  25 年、營收持續增加，且
璟德自行設計之比重逐年提高。產能充裕、稼動率仍低，成長無
產能瓶頸。  
公司處分舊廠後遷入新廠，目前稼動率僅約  5~6 成，現有產能足
以支應未來數年成長 。 減資方面 ， 公司於26Q2 完成現金減資  3 億
元、減資率  43.5% ，股本由  6.9 億元降至  3.9 億元，旨在優化
資產結構、提高股本運用效率並回饋股東；減資後帳上現金充裕、
淨利率仍維持約  26% ，營運結構更為輕量。

2.已切入低軌衛星寬頻供應鏈，營收貢獻有待成長  
低軌衛星是近年成長最快的產業之一，據  TrendForce ，受惠衛星
寬頻、手機直連與  AI 太空運算需求，預估  2027 年全球衛星產
業產值將達  4,470 億美元。事實上它分為兩條截然不同的應用與
供應鏈：一是「衛星寬頻」 ，衛星透過  Ku ／Ka 頻段，把網路送
到地面接收站 (Gateway ，地面閘道站 )與用戶碟形天線；二是「手
機直連」，衛星作為太空基地台，用行動電話頻段 (1.9GHz) 直接連
手機。璟德聚焦衛星寬頻鏈路中的高頻射頻元件，分為兩塊：地
面端為地面接收站所需之  LTCC 濾波器，已實際出貨；衛星本體

端為  Ka 頻段的收發 (Tx ／Rx) 天線陣列模組依其  2025 年開發清
單 ， 公司已完成發射(8.8×8.8mm) 與接收 (13.2×13.2mm) 兩款雙圓極
化天線陣列及相關基板材料，目前仍與數家夥伴送樣驗證。璟德
並非直接供貨予終端美系大廠，而是攜手長期合作關係的夥伴一
同打入供應鏈等地面站供應鏈，即扮演  LTCC 元件與材料供應
商，由中游模組廠整合為地面站設備或衛星酬載後，再交付營運
商；低軌衛星為長線里程碑、短期難以量化。公司射頻濾波元件
已切入低軌衛星 (與美系大廠合作，  FR2 ／FR3 相關應用亦在進
行)；即使於特定專案市占率高，總量市場還有很大的成長空間，
對整體營收之貢獻仍有限。後續可觀察衛星本體天線陣列的驗證
進度，以及隨在軌衛星數量與  6G 頻段增加所帶動的  LTCC 用
量，能否讓這塊藉由高市佔率貢獻營收。

3.WiFi 穩固，車載、國防、智慧基建等寬頻相關逐步成長   
WiFi 為公司營運基本盤，每台裝置的高頻濾波／前端模組含量隨
規格升級而提升。隨著技術迭代升級 WiFi 7 每台終端所需之濾波
器、雙工器與天線模組數量增加，惟一般家庭頻寬利用率偏低，
供應鏈價格相對穩定。車載方面，單車感測器數量隨  ADAS ／雷
達滲透持續上升， 2026 年起車用感測元件用量明顯增加；國防相
關需求則受地緣情勢與各國國防現代化帶動而強勁，例如 14GHz 
軍工收發、 8/12GHz 軍工接收之帶通濾波器，以及  8/14GHz 軍
工收發高抑制雙工器，對應  X ／Ku 頻段 (8~14GHz) 之軍用雷達、
通訊與電子作戰前端，受各國國防現代化帶動而需求強勁。；智
慧城市與智慧抄表亦提供穩定的  LPWAN 需求。此三者共同特徵
為「高可靠、高單價、 Design-in 後長期出貨」，恰是  LTCC 高層
數模組發展性佳的應用領域，與璟德的技術定位高度契合。

叁、業 績 及 獲 利 預 估

一、 2Q26 營收谷底回升，寬頻新應用驅動營運轉型

璟德  2Q26 營收  4.06 億元， QoQ +15.3% 、YoY +13.7% ，帶動  
1H26 營收  7.58 億元 、YoY +2.1%， 為單月營收自 2025 年 3 月
起連續  13 個月年減後首度在 2Q26 轉正，月營收由約  1.1 億元
谷底回升至  5 月之  1.36 億元 (YoY +17.6%) 。 獲利方面 ，2Q26 毛
利率  44.3% 、 營業利益率 29.8% 、 稅後淨利率 25% ， 單季稅後 EPS 
1.47 元， 1H26 累計  2.86 元(減資前股本 6.9 億元計算 )。營收結
構上，2Q26 寬頻新應用占  58% 、Wi-Fi 33% 、手機  9% ，較 1H25 
之 40% ／41% ／19% 大幅轉向高單價之寬頻新應用；以絕對金額
計， 1H26 寬頻營收  4.32 億元、 YoY +45% ，Wi-Fi 2.50 億元、
YoY −18%，手機  0.76 億元、 YoY −46%，區域亦同步由中國轉向
北美 (1H26 北美占比達  52%) 。 
二、2025 年廠房一次性獲利 ，2026 年回歸本業搭配減資 EPS
上升  
2025 年帳列  EPS 9.42 元含處分廠房之一次性業外利益（稅後約  
3.5 億元）， 屬不可延續之獲利 ， 還原後 2025 年本業  EPS 約 4.4 
元 。就本業而言，2026 年起回到公司自谷底回升 、 產品組合轉佳，
2026 年本業稅後淨利較  2025 年本業約  YoY+29% ，動能明確向
上。此外，公司已於 26Q2 完成現金減資 (減資率  43.5% 、每股退
還 4.3468 元)，流通股數由  6,902 萬股縮減至  3,902 萬股、新
股 6/30 重新交易；本益比不因減資改變，每股盈餘因股數減少而
墊高， 26Q3 起 EPS 採減資後股數計算 (換算約  ×1.769) 。

營 運 分 析 
台灣具代表性的磁性元件廠，產品聚焦功率電感與濾波器  
臺慶科技成立於 1983 年，總部位於桃園，為台灣主要磁性元件製造商之一，
產品涵蓋功率電感、線圈、濾波器及變壓器。公司具備從磁性材料配方、鐵氧
體與金屬粉末成形，到自動繞線及封裝的垂直整合能力，可依客戶需求提供高
可靠度與客製化產品。 
產品以電源電感為主，營收占比約六成，共模、網路濾波器及繞線式訊號電感
約二成，積層晶片磁珠與電感約 18%。26Q1 應用別以車用電子 38%為最大
宗，其次為 PC 24%、網通 16%、AI 相關 12%及消費性電子 9%；AI 伺服器
已自 PC應用中獨立計列。 
公司主要生產據點位於中國昆山及泗洪，負責積層晶片磁珠、共模濾波器與繞
線電感等核心產品量產；廣東東莞則提供在地技術及客戶服務。馬來西亞柔佛
新廠導入自動化產線，定位為網通、車用及高可靠度電感的第二量產基地。 
銷售模式約各有三分之一來自直接客戶、代理商及貼牌業務。2025 年私募引
進美商柏恩斯控股，柏恩斯為公司主要貼牌客戶及最大單一客戶，營收占比約
16%至 17%，策略入股後有機會增加貼牌訂單。公司另持有新加坡同業
SuperO 23.5%，藉其據點接觸歐美客戶及雲端服務供應商。

26Q1 獲利率優於預期，第二季營收預估突破 20 億元 
臺慶科 26Q1 營收 17.35 億元（QoQ -3.9%／YoY +11.3%） ，毛利率28.9%
（QoQ +0.4ppt／YoY +3.3ppt） ，營業利益2.59億元、營業利益率 14.9%，
稅後純益 2.86 億元（QoQ +12.0%／YoY +27.3%），EPS 2.51 元。26Q1營
收受到 2 月工作天數較少影響，但產能利用率及產品組合改善，使毛利率與
營業利益率優於原先預期。 
4 月及 5 月營收分別達 7.40 億元及 7.09 億元，連續創下單月歷史新高，達
標時間早於原先預期的第三季旺季，主要來自車用與 AI需求同步成長。6月
因客戶於 25 日前後進行年中盤點，收貨天數縮短，單月營收可能較 4、5月
回落，但 26Q2仍維持明顯季增。 
研究部預估 26Q2 營收 20.18 億元（QoQ +16.3%／YoY +25.3%） ，毛利率
29.2%，營業利益率 15.2%，稅後純益 3.52 億元，EPS 3.07元；26Q3 營收
21.46 億元（QoQ +6.3%／YoY +30.2%） ，毛利率30.2%，稅後純益 3.67
億元，EPS 3.19 元。公司維持 Q3＞Q2＞Q1 的方向，Q4 能見度須待 9 月
後確認，研究部暫估 26Q4 營收高檔持平於 20.92 億元，EPS 3.22元。

九成稼動率已近滿載，毛利改善主力為產品組合而非調價 
公司整體接單量約相當於產能的 120%，標準交期約八週，平均稼動率約九
成，其中晶片電感高於名目產能，一體成形電感亦接近滿載，訊號電感相對
較低。由於電感產品料號、尺寸、模具及繞線規格繁多，產線需頻繁換線，
九成稼動率已代表生產處於高檔，營收規模擴大可有效降低固定成本。 
毛利率改善主要來自車用及 AI 等高毛利產品占比增加。車用與 AI 產品因材
料、測試及可靠度要求較高，毛利率估高於35%；PC 及消費性產品約 25%，
網通約 20%。隨車用占比維持約四成、AI占比由 10%提高至 14%至 15%，

個股報告 
整體產品組合持續改善。 
研究部預估 2026 年毛利率 29.4%，較 2025 年的 26.4%提高 3.0ppt，營業
費用率由 14.3%降至 13.9%，帶動營業利益率由12.0%提高至 15.5%。2027
年毛利率進一步提高至 30.3%，費用率降至 13.5%，營業利益率達 16.8%。 
公司自 2025 年 9 月起因銀價快速上升，對銀材用量較高的晶片磁珠及晶片
電感進行滾動式調價，2026 年 4月起則陸續調整部分繞線式訊號電感價格。
然而，電源電感占營收六成以上，其中一體成形電感並非本波漲價的主要產
品，因此調價以轉嫁原料成本為主，毛利率上修仍主要來自稼動率及產品組
合。 
AI 營收主力為電源模組與加速卡，TLVR為後續成長選項 
AI相關營收目前以電源模組、AI加速卡及網通加速器供應鏈為主，其中部分
加速卡專案為單一供應，高壓直流供電（HVDC）則因安規與可靠度門檻較
高，導入後供應商不易更換；直接用於伺服器主機板的產品多設有第二供應
商，訂單分配仍取決於價格、品質與交期。主機板電壓調節模組所用的一體
成形電感目前月出貨約 500 萬至 600 萬顆、現階段營收貢獻高於 TLVR，並
隨 AI 伺服器與 ASIC 平台增加而續增。TLVR 主要用於 GPU 旁供電、單一
機櫃用量可達 1,000 顆以上 、 新品單價約25至 30元／顆 ， 惟現有月產能500
萬顆尚未滿載，部分CSP雖已完成產品承認，仍待平台開案與代工廠發包，
加以美、日、台系多家已通過認證，研究部不將 TLVR 列為 2026 年首要成
長來源。平台進度上，ASIC專案較快、最快 26Q3 貢獻，Rubin相關已切入
部分專案、量產最快落在 2026 年底並可能遞延至 2027 年；因此 2026 年
AI成長主要來自既有電源模組、加速卡與主機板產品，TLVR 與 Rubin 支撐
後續成長。

- 5 - 
個股報告

車用維持獲利支柱，馬來西亞廠下半年起貢獻 
車用電子占營收約 38%至 40%，應用涵蓋電源、自動駕駛、車燈與胎壓偵測；
車用產品須符合較長使用年限與嚴格的材料、製程及可靠度測試，客戶導入
後不易更換供應商，毛利率與訂單能見度均高於一般消費性產品，構成獲利
結構的主要支柱。馬來西亞廠已於 2025 年下半年通過美系網通大廠認證、
2026 年 5 月通過美系電動車客戶產品認證，實際交貨仍待該廠 7 月取得車
規品質系統認證；下半年營收貢獻可望逐步增加，中長期占比目標約一成，
除支援車用客戶外、亦可因應美系網通與 AI客戶的非中國產能需求。

DDR5 與微型一體成形電感提供明確數量成長 
DDR5較 DDR4增加電源管理元件需求 、 單一應用約使用3至 4顆電源電感 。
臺慶科相關產品月出貨量由 2025 年的 700 萬至 800 萬顆提高至 2026 年的
1,000 萬顆以上、全年估成長三成；其中供 AI 伺服器者列入 AI 應用、其餘
歸入 PC，故 DDR5成長並非全數反映於 AI營收。公司並持續擴充微型一體
成形電感（mini molding） ，單價雖低於大型一體成形電感，但可因應終端微
型化與功率密度提高、現階段產能接近滿載。相較TLVR仍待後續平台發包，
DDR5與 mini molding 均已實際出貨，為 2026 年較具能見度的成長來源。

CB 稀釋壓低 EPS增幅，AI與車用支撐本業高成長 
研究部預估臺慶科 2026 年營收 79.91 億元 （YoY +20.6%） 、毛利率29.4%、
營業利益 12.40 億元（YoY +56.1%） 、稅後純益13.76 億元（YoY +30.3%）；
2027 年營收 96.43 億元（YoY +20.7%） ，受惠AI電源模組、主機板一體成
形電感、ASIC與 Rubin相關專案擴大，以及馬來西亞廠車用產品貢獻增加，
毛利率提高至 30.3%、營業利益16.19 億元 （YoY +30.6%） 、稅後純益16.31
億元（YoY +18.6%）。 
考量剩餘可轉債陸續轉換，研究部將普通股股本假設由 2025 年的 11.06 億
元提高至 2026 年的 11.49億元，2027 年再增至 11.99億元，使2026／2027
年 EPS分別為 11.97元／13.60 元；若股本維持 11.06億元，EPS 應分別為
12.44 元／14.75 元，累計稀釋約 0.47 元／1.15 元，顯示 EPS 增幅低於稅
後純益主要反映股本擴大，而非本業成長放緩。考量車用與AI 高毛利產品占
比持續提升、營業利益連兩年成長逾三成，並以部分AI加速卡專案的單一供
應地位及 HVDC後續切入機會為支撐 ， 研究部給予目標價 354元(26X 2027F 
PER)，潛在上漲空間 22.1%，維持「逢低買進」評等。

壹、投 資 建 議

一. 預估 2Q26 稅後 EPS 1.13 元 
日成 KY 04~05/2026 營收金額 1.73 億元與 2.15 億元，年增率
47.28% 與 48.79% ，推估日成 KY 2Q26 營收金額 6.18 億元，
YoY+35.3% ，QoQ+0.5% ，預估營業利益 0.55 億元，較 2Q25 虧
轉盈， QoQ-36.9% ，預估稅後盈餘 0.55 億元，較 2Q25 虧轉盈，
QoQ-17.06% ，預估稅後 EPS 1.13 元。

二. 預估 3Q26 稅後 EPS 1.92 元 
在訂單維持滿載，電鍍產能提升兩班制，預估日成 KY 3Q26 營收
金額 6.86 億元， YoY+9.93% ，QoQ+11.00% ，預估營業利益 0.95
億元， YoY+183.18% ，QoQ+71.55% ，預估稅後盈餘 0.94 億元，
YoY+333.00% ，QoQ+70.29% ，預估稅後 EPS 1.92 元。

三. 預估 2026 年稅後 EPS 5.00 元 
日成 KY 2026 年在主要客戶受到銀價上漲，新產品規劃以鉑金產
品為大宗 ， 其中日成KY 電鍍產能在經濟規模與品質良率受惠客戶
新產品訂單較大份額，將帶動營收成長；在獲利方面，在產品組
合優化與調整代工費帶動毛利率提升，進而帶動獲利成長。宏遠
預估日成 KY 2026 年營收金額 25.00 億元， YoY+17.47% ，預估
營業利益 2.69 億元， YoY+870.02% ，預估稅後盈餘 2.45 億元，
由虧轉盈，預估稅後 EPS 5.00 元。

四. 預估 2027 年稅後 EPS 6.50 元 
日成 KY 2027 年在主要客戶新產品推出，刺激下游終端需求回
溫，進而推升主要客戶訂單維持高檔水準，其餘客戶方面，受惠
滲透率提升與拓展新地區業務，綜合上述，日成 2027 年營運維持
成長態勢。宏遠預估日成 KY 2027 年營收金額 28.00 億元，
YoY+12.00% ，預估營業利益 3.26 億元， YoY+21.44% ，預估稅
後盈餘 3.18 億元， YoY+29.9% ，預估稅後 EPS 6.50 元。

貳、公 司 營 運 概 況

一.公司簡介 
日成控股成立於 1989 年，資本額 4.90 億元，並於 2017 年掛牌
上市，日成控股為流行珠寶及飾品設計製造出口企業，初期公司
名為日成有限公司。 1991 年公司更名為日成珠寶製造股份有限公
司，經過數年的經營，生產規模擴大，生產工藝及設計能力深受
國際客戶喜愛，並在當地珠寶及飾品設計製造產業享負盛名。有
鑑於公司成長及管理需求，積極推動專業管理方式，於 2003 獲得  
ISO 9001 認證。另，於 2004 年導入  ERP 系統，以因應公司未
來業務需求，快速成長趨勢，資源整合，以達有效管理及運用。
科技日新月異，日成公司為滿足客戶要求，不斷增強研發能力，
於 2007 年大量投入具有較強的設計能力及使用最先進的技術 ， 已
拓展生產能方面機器，如沖壓鑄造、金屬多樣鑄臺，並軟體以及
使用 3D 設計技術軟件等，設計出時尚與滿足客戶需求之產品。

圖一、日成控股身處產業中游地位

資料來源：公司、宏遠投顧整理

二. 2026 年營運概況及展望  
日成 -KY 主要營業項目為珠寶首飾設計、製造與銷售，產品包含
吊墜、戒指、耳環、手環、手鍊、項鍊與服飾配件等，主要生產
基地位於泰國曼谷近郊的龍仔厝，基地面積 6.59 萬平方米，員工
人數在 3100 人，滿載月產值在 2~2.5 億元。日成主要客戶多為國
際精品大廠，銷售區域遍布歐美亞三大洲，且日成控股泰國工廠
規模符合國際品牌代工條件，標準化生產製程具效率，且具有
ODM 設計開發能力。此外，公司也是泰國少數同時具有大規模產
能及電鍍產線的 ODM 代工廠。

圖二、珠寶產業分佈

資料來源：公司、宏遠投顧整理

觀察全球主要珠寶品牌商受到白銀價格大幅上漲侵蝕利潤與下游
終端客戶需求，因此將加速鉑金  (Platinum) 系列的轉型與推廣，
以多樣化產品線應對成本波動。為降低對白銀的依賴，計畫將部
分暢銷產品從銀製改為鍍鉑金設計，同時將產品線中銀製品的比
例從約 60% 降至 20% ，並希望在 2028 年前完成此轉型。由於鉑
金價格遠高於白銀，因此會在合金基底上鍍鉑金，既可減少鉑金
使用量，也有助控制成本，最終售價與銀製品相同，將有助廠商
降低銀價上漲侵蝕利潤的情況。

日成 KY 01~05/2025 營收金額 10.03 億元， YoY+27.32% 。日成
2025 年營運動能主要包括： 1，全球珠寶產業在 2022~2023 年經
歷後疫情時代庫存調整， 2024 年己有止穩並小幅回升情況， 2025
年在產業景氣持續回升，加上新材料實驗室鑽石價格也跌至甜蜜
點，品牌商將積極開發實驗室鑽石珠寶，有助整體產業 2026 年持
續回溫。 2，觀察第一大客戶 2021~2025 年營收占比，除 2023 年
占比 29% 較低外，其餘年度營收占比落在 43~52% ，在珠寶市場
己開始轉型鉑金產品，在電鍍加工的效率與良率將成為製程關
鍵，日成在電鍍品質與產能為泰國優秀廠商，預期在第一大客戶
在新產品推出帶動下， 2026 年營收將戶長 35~40% 。3，在澳洲
區新客戶 (經營 3 年多 )與北美新客戶 (經營兩年多 )在多年來的深耕
經營與合作默契培養，預期 2026 年新客戶營收占比將有明顯提
升。預估日成 KY 2026 年營收金額 25.00 億元， YoY+17.47% 。

預期 2027 年，在原有客戶產品改款帶動下游需求熱絡，預期第一
大客戶 2027 年營收將小幅成長 10~15% ，其餘客戶方面，受惠滲
透率提升與新地區業務開拓帶動下 ， 預期2027 年營收成長幅度將
落在 15~20% 。綜合上述，預估日成 KY 2027 年營收金額 28.00
億元， YoY+12.00% 。

中國需求優於預期，上修 2Q26 獲利 
胡連 2Q26營收 27.5億元 (QoQ +29%/YoY+27%)，優於預期，動能來自中
國市場營收回溫 (YoY+22%)；加上非中國地區 (YoY+45%) 受惠於美國鏟雪
車客戶需求復甦、歐洲機車線束需求強勁。毛利率方面，隨高頻高壓產品出
貨帶動產品組合優化與稼動率提升，然原料成本 (銅、塑料) 處於高檔，且公
司無法完全轉嫁成本，故維持 2Q26 毛利率預估 27.3% (QoQ+0.7ppt/YoY -
6.2ppt) 。然隨營收規模放大，上修營業利益 12%至 3.3 億元  
(QoQ+81%/YoY-15%)、上修 EPS 5%至 2.16元 (QoQ+35%/YoY+184%)。 
歐洲新品開始出貨將挹注 3Q26 營運動能 
展望 3Q26，中國市場能見度已至 8月，估營收年增幅有望達 20%；非中國
市場營收年增幅估 48%，其中以歐美市場表現較為強勁，受惠於 EPDU 上
蓋部件開始出貨，及美國鏟雪車需求續強，故本中心上修 3Q26 營收 8%至
29 億元 (QoQ+6%/YoY+25%)，毛利率方面， 2Q26 LME 平均銅價仍季增
4%，惟 3Q26 稼動率及產品組合持續轉佳， 故維持毛利率預估之 28.2% 
(QoQ+0.9ppt/YoY-1.4ppt)；隨營收規模放大，上修營業利益 11%至 3.9 億
元(QoQ+20%/ YoY+21%)；預估上修 EPS 6%至 2.57元。 
海外產能與新品驅動 2027 年獲利動能轉強 
上修 2026年營收 2%至 111億元(YoY+13%)，儘管中國車市偏弱，仍受惠
客戶新品量產及非中市場雙位數成長，支撐全年營收動能；惟 1Q26 獲利較
弱，故下修 EPS至 9.83元(YoY-9%)。展望 2027年，中國市場受惠於高頻
高速、PCB保險絲盒等新品貢獻，海外則受惠越南廠供應美系電動車客戶連
接器、印尼廠 BYD 保險絲盒量產、高頻高速產能擴張支應客戶需求。本中
心預估 2027 年營收 127 億元  (YoY + 14%)， EPS 上修至 13.08 元 
(YoY+33%) 。考量 2027年客戶需求明確，且目前評價處歷史低檔，給予目
標價 150元，基於 2027年 EPS、本益比則維持於 11倍，調升評等至買進。 
元大觀點 
⧫  
2Q26 中國市場需求回溫，客戶啟動回補庫存，加上非中國地區受惠美
國鏟雪車客戶需求復甦、歐洲市場機車線束需求強勁，上修獲利 5%。 
⧫  
3Q26 中國與非中國市場展望俱佳，中國市場營收預期將年增 達 20%；
非中市場亦受惠新品出貨、鏟雪車客戶需求續強，上修獲利 6%。 
⧫  
展望 2027 年，海外產能與新品驅動獲利動能轉強，上修目標價至 150
元 (11x 2027F EPS)，並調升評等至買進。

銅價維持高檔，將壓抑 2026 年毛利率 
胡連產品主要使用的原物料為銅及塑料，分別約佔銷貨成本 35%/30%，胡連之毛利率表現與 LME
銅價波動呈現顯著的遞延效應，時間差約落於 2-3 個月(即約 1個季度)，主因公司為因應龐大料號
(SKU)與急單需求，長期維持約 100-130 天的庫存水位(含原物料、在製品與成品)，使當期銷貨成
本反映的是約一季前的原料採購價格。在銅價上漲週期，受惠於低價庫存效益，公司短期毛利率往
往不降反升；反之，當銅價反轉下跌時，因需優先去化先前建立的高價庫存，毛利率回升將出現滯
後，甚至面臨短期庫存跌價損失壓力。雖公司與 Tier 1 及大型 OEM客戶簽有原物料連動條款，但
調價機制並非即時反應，通常採季度或半年度檢視均價後進行 ASP 調整。因此，在原料急漲期間，
成本轉嫁存在約一季的時間差，需待下個議價週期生效後，獲利結構方能回復常軌。  
鑑於中國車廠客戶強勢，轉嫁原物料漲價空間有限，透過以下策略， 2026 年毛利率可望緩解衝擊：
1) 銅價上漲對純端子產品衝擊最顯著，故提升單價較高、技術附加價值大且受銅價波動影響較小的
高頻高壓產品比重；2) 透過擴大經濟規模及內部自動化、尋求替代料以稀釋成本壓力；綜合上述，
預估 2026/2027年毛利率 28.1%/30.1%，YoY-3.4ppt/+2.0ppt。

東莞新廠預估 1Q27 完工後投產，以支應中國內需市場 
胡連 2026年資本支出規劃為 16億元，其中約 5億元用於東莞廠建廠(2025年即啟動，2026年進
入工程款支付高峰期)，約 10-11 億元主要分配於支付台北總部大樓尾款以及模具與自動化設備之
添購。東莞廠預計於 1Q27 完工後正式投產並貢獻營收，未來東莞新廠將全數用於滿足中國內需市
場及比亞迪初期出口至歐洲的訂單，非中國地區需求則主要由台灣及東南亞廠區支應。隨著新廠建
設與設備資本化，預估 2026全年折舊攤提費用將落在 4-5億元區間。目前產能區域比重約為中國
58%、台灣 22%、越南 15%、印尼 5%。 
2026 年中國市場谷底已過，非中國市場成長動能強勁 
1Q26胡連於中國市場營收年減約 14%，主因購置稅減半退場與季節性因素，為全年谷底；自 4月
起年增幅轉正，5-8月掌握狀況明顯改善，客戶進入庫存回補階段。2026年中國車市含出口整體恐
仍小幅衰退，惟胡連受惠客戶新品陸續量產，中國銷售表現預期明顯優於車市：1) 高頻高速以中國
自主品牌為主要客戶， BYD 高頻取得新定點（取代非中國供應商），國產替代由低壓 產品延伸至
高頻高壓產品；2)上汽、長安已完整 PCB保險絲盒導入，2026年營收目標 5億元；3) 其他增量產
品包含座椅線束、小線纜、電動座椅連接器等。綜合上述，本中心預估中國市場 2026年營收 86.1
億元(YoY+7.7%)，營收佔比 77.3%。 
歐洲市場方面，胡連採策略合作、專案客戶、與股權投資並進模式， 2026 年成長動能包含 1)與
Lear合作之 JLR (Jaguar Land Rover) 專案，胡連負責供應 EPDU上蓋部件，並非整顆 PDU，預
計 3Q26開始量產出貨；2) 既有歐洲客戶 Piaggio (比亞久)電動小型商用車之 PDU (高壓配電盒)以
及機車線束新產品；3) 併購兩家位於北非、突尼西亞設廠的汽車線束及農耕機具線束公司，主要生
產高毛利的高端線束與跨足農用車市場，預估於 2H26 開始併入財務報表，可望帶動胡連連接器產
品進入歐洲通路並優化整體產品組合。綜合上述，本中心預估歐洲市場 2026 年營收 3.7 億元
(YoY+70.9%)，營收佔比 3.3%。 
除了中國及歐洲市場外，其餘海外市場受惠： 1) 台灣地區主要銷售汽機車線束產品， 2026 年預估
新增兩家車廠客戶，分別銷售線束及高頻+低壓連接器，同時亦確認工廠自動化與無人搬運車 (AGN)
客戶之連接器需求，惟目前仍在初期階段，規模較小，本中心預估台灣市場 2026 年營收 4.8 億元
(YoY+18.3%)，營收佔比 4.3%；2) 美國受惠鏟雪車客戶線束需求明顯回溫及 PCB 保險絲盒自
2025 年送驗完成後 於 2026 年銷售逐步放量 ，本中心預估美國市場 2026 年營收 5.8 億元
(YoY+69.3%)，營收佔比 5.2%；3) 已向 BYD提供 PCB保險絲盒樣品並試裝，規劃將南京廠相關
設備移至印尼廠，預計 9M26完成產線建置待客戶驗廠，並於 4Q26開始投產，本中心預估印尼市
場 2026年營收 3.03億元(YoY+34.5%)，營收佔比 2.7%；4) 越南廠預估 10M26開始小批量交貨
10餘項低壓連接器產品予美國電動車客戶之非中國市場，本中心預估越南市場 2026年營收 2.6億
元(YoY+40.8%)，營收佔比 2.3%。

產業概況
2026 年中國汽車補貼轉向比例激勵機制，推動中高階車款換購
2026 年汽車補貼政策延續以舊換新策略，由「定額補貼」轉為「按車價比例」的結構性激勵，重
點支持中高階車款。補貼最高可達人民幣 2萬元，目的為削減低價車款的依賴，推動高技術車型，
並從 2026 年起恢復新能源汽車車輛購置稅，但維持 5%的減半優惠。報廢購買方面，若消費者報
廢乘用車符合特定條件，並購買新能源乘用車或排碳量較低的燃油車，則能夠獲得一次性定額補貼，
補貼額度介於 1.5-2 萬元人民幣之間，一年最多申請一次。中汽協初步測算，享受補貼的乘用車有
望超過 1,200萬輛，可望拉動新車銷售近 150萬輛，預估 2026年汽車以舊換新政策受惠人數將高
於 2025年。

政策調整
2026年 1月 1日至 2027年 12月 31日，新能源汽車不再全免，改為「減半徵收」車輛購置稅，實際稅率由0%調整
為 5%，並且設限每輛新能源乘用車減免稅額不超過 1.5 萬元人民幣。
資料來源：中汽協、元大投顧
2025 年全球乘用車銷量約 8,500 萬輛，年增 3%，2026 年估僅小幅年增 0.7%
全球汽車乘用車於 2018年開始衰退；2020年受到疫情影響為谷底(年減 13%)；2021開始復甦(年
增 3%)；2022 年逢車用晶片短缺、疫情造成供應鏈不順等負面影響(年減 3%)；2023 年全球汽車

銷售車用晶片缺料緩解，基期較低(大幅年增 12%)；2024年全球乘用車增速將放緩(年增 2%)。
2025 年全球汽車乘用車銷量約 8,500 萬輛，年增 3%，其中中國 /歐洲 /美國乘用車銷量分別
YoY+9%/+2%/+2%。
➢ 中國：乘用車銷量 3,006萬輛，年增 9%，受惠 1) 設備更新與以舊換新政策擴大實施；2) 中
國汽車出口總量達 709.8 萬輛(年增 21.1%)，快速搶佔全球市場；3) 中國品牌乘用車銷量比
重提升 4.3ppts至接近 70%。1-5M26乘用車銷量 1,032萬輛，YoY-6%，主因補貼退場使國
內零售轉弱，惟出口表現仍強勁，部分緩解產能壓力。
➢ 歐洲：乘用車銷量 1,327萬輛，年增 2%，其中純電動車新車銷量(佔比 22.6%)於 2025/12正
式超越燃油車(佔比 22.5%)，主因歐盟下令 2025年起，新車碳排放需較 2021年減少 15%，
未達標企業面臨 95歐元/每克二氧化碳的罰款，迫使車廠加大電動車投放。1-5M26乘用車銷

量 583 萬輛，YoY+5%，主要受惠電動車銷量大幅增長，市佔率近 20%，主要受惠德國、英
國電動車需求強勁。
➢ 美國：儘管面臨高通膨、進口關稅上升、電動車補貼退場等不利因素，惟豐田及現代汽車在
美國銷量受惠經濟型汽車及混和動力車普及，以及通用汽車受惠大型皮卡、 SUV 及電動車銷
量推動，相抵銷下美國乘用車銷量仍微幅年增 2%至 1,625萬輛。1-5M26乘用車銷量 649萬
輛，YoY-5%，主因 1) 隨電動車購車稅務抵減到期，電動車銷量年減近三成；2) 美國聯準會
維持較高利率水平，推升汽車貸款成本。

展望後市，本中心預估 2026 年全球乘用車銷量小幅年增 0.7%，預估中國 /歐洲 /美國分別
YoY+0.2%/+2.1%/-1.7%。1) 中國乘聯會預估 2026 年汽車市場仍處於築底、緩慢復甦之格局，主
因內需疲軟、部分地方政府面臨財政壓力，縮減或暫停汽車「以舊換新」補貼、修訂後的國家補貼
計畫將固定補貼改為比例補貼等，而隨著全球石油價格回落、歐洲及北美對電動車補貼調整以及關
稅壁壘上升，2026 年純電動車出口增速將放緩；2) 歐洲市場成長主要來自電動車需求延續、排放
合規要求放寬及在地化生產要求，惟考量佔比高達六成的企業車隊採購意願因換車週期延長 而維持
低迷，加上工業活動與貿易環境仍存不確定性將壓抑成長性；3) 預估美國市場衰退，主因受川普政
府關稅政策、電動車購車稅務抵減到期、保險費用及維修成本攀升影響消費者購車意願。

2025 年全球新能源車銷量 2,218 萬輛，年增 26%，2026 年估放緩至年增 8% 
2025年全球新能源車銷量 2,218萬輛(年增 26%)，滲透率 26.1% (年增 4.6ppts)，其中主要市場分
別為美國 147萬輛(年減 6%)、歐洲 386萬輛(年增 31%)、中國 1,644萬輛(年增 28%)、其他地區
42 萬輛(年增 10%)，1) 美國市場受稅收抵免政策到期與關稅政策搖擺使銷量僅小幅成長；2) 歐洲
市場受惠歐盟排放法規趨嚴促使車廠加速推出多樣化、平價化車款，搭配中國品牌 (如比亞迪、名
爵)低價搶攻與成熟的充電基建； 3) 中國市場受惠高性價比產品帶動內需，加上政策補貼的最後拉
力，導致新能源車市佔率首度超越燃油車。1-5M26 美國新能源車銷量 65 萬輛，年減 15%，主要
受 IRA補貼退場影響；歐洲新能源車銷量 165萬輛，YoY+15%，年增受惠於義大利、法國、德國
於年初啟動新一輪針對節能車款的稅收獎勵計畫；中國新能源車銷量 580萬輛，YoY+4%，新能源
車款相對整體市場較強。 
展望 2026年新能源車銷量，1) 美國市場受聯邦政府取消 7,500 美元稅收抵免(2025/9終止)及燃油
效率標準放寬的影響，銷量預估年減 0.3%；2) 歐洲市場受惠歐盟碳排放目標收緊及新補貼政策推
動，銷量預估年增 18%；3) 中國市場雖面臨補貼金額縮減及經濟增速放緩，惟以舊換新補貼改採
比例制精準對接老舊車輛的更新需求，加上城區智駕 (車子進入市區後，能自動識別紅綠燈、避讓
行人與外送車、自動繞障等)技術全面下放至 15 萬級距車型、混動技術對燃油車份額的加速替代，
以及中國本土品牌外銷持續提升，銷量預估年增 9%。綜合之下，本中心預估 2026 年全球新能源
車銷量 2,392萬輛(年增 8%)，滲透率達 28.1% (年增 2.0ppts)。

獲利調整與股票評價
谷底已過，海外產能與新品驅動 2027 年獲利動能轉強，調升為買進
展望 2026 年，1Q26為全年谷底、2Q-4Q26逐季成長。地區別方面，中國車市 2026年含出口整
體恐仍小幅衰退，惟胡連受惠客戶新品量產，中國市場銷售表現預期明顯優於整體車市；非中國市
場則預估雙位數年增，預估受惠 1) 歐洲新增與 Lear合作，由其組裝出貨的 JLR與 Volvo專案、歐
洲客戶 Piaggio (比亞久)機車線束新產品、併購兩家位於北非及突尼西亞設廠的汽車線束及農耕機
具線束公司(預估 2H26 可完成併表並認列營收)；2) 新增兩位車廠客戶(分別銷售線束及高頻+低壓
連接器)；3) 美國鏟雪車客戶線束需求回溫並新增 PCB保險絲盒訂單；4) 10M26 越南廠開始小批
量生產低壓產品給美國電動車客戶的非中國市場；5) 印尼廠預計於 4Q26開始供應 PCB保險絲盒
給 BYD印尼新廠。綜合上述，預估上修胡連 2026年營收 1.9%至 111.4億元(YoY+13.4%)。

展望 2027年，中國部分，公司將提升高頻高速、PCB等新品銷售，降低對低壓連接器的依賴。此
外，中國自給產能緊張，公司將擴建東莞二廠，預期 1Q27 完工，將可支應中國需求。本中心預估
2027 年中國營收將年增 13%；海外部分，預期胡連將受惠產能貢獻放大與新品比重持續提升，預
估海外營收將年增 18%，受惠於 1) 越南廠供應美國電動車客戶之連接器自 10M26 小批量起量，
2027年月銷售額有望提升至 3,000萬元 (目前約 2,000萬元)；2) 印尼 BYD保險絲盒將自 4Q26投
產後於 2027年放量，越南、印尼廠仍有相當大擴充空間，可於既有廠房增加設備因應；3) 歐洲兩
家併購企業將於 2027年提供歐洲當地產能與線束能力，支應 BYD匈牙利廠等中系客戶歐洲需求；
綜合上述，預估上修 2027年營收 5.0%至 126.8億元(YoY+13.8%)。
1Q26/2Q26 LME銅價已攀升至每噸$12,891/$13,385，惟胡連透過優化產品組合(2026年高頻高壓

連接器產品營收預估 YoY+76%，佔比自 5%提升至 8-9%)及尋求替代料以稍微緩解成本壓力，惟
1Q26 受中國市場拖累 (1Q26 毛利率 26.6%，QoQ-4.5ppt/YoY-5.1ppt)，故下修 2026 年毛利率
0.9ppt至 28.1% (YoY -3.3ppt)，下修 EPS 2.8%至 9.83元(YoY-8.5%)；維持 2027年預估毛利率
30.1%(YoY+2.0ppt)，上修 EPS 1.2%至 13.08元 (YoY+33.1%)。
胡連過去 3年平均本益比位於 8-17倍，目前位於 2026年 EPS的 9.4倍本益比，屬於歷史區間偏
低水位。展望後市，儘管 2026 年獲利仍受高價銅成本壓抑，且 2026 年中國車市預估小幅衰退，
惟胡連受惠主要客戶新品陸續量產與高頻高壓產品國產替代定點，中國市場銷售表現優於整體車市，
4月起中國營收年增已轉正，2Q26年增約 20%，本中心認為 1Q26營收已確立谷底，2-4Q26將逐
季成長，且 2027年成長動能明確。考量胡連營運動能自 2027年起明顯轉強，本中心維持 11倍本

益比，以 2027年 EPS 13.08元，給予目標價 150元，調升胡連至買進評等。

公司簡介  
胡連成立於 1977年，以金屬沖壓端子零件起家，後發展塑膠連接器產品，現為汽機車專業連接器廠商。胡連 1Q26產品比
重為：塑件 36%、端子 28%、保險絲盒 13%、線束 9%、板端件 6%、高壓+高頻 6%、其他 2%。胡連目前主要以提供中
國車廠客戶為主，1Q26客戶區域別比重為：中國 77%、台灣 5%、越南 2%、印尼 3%、歐洲 3%、美洲 5%、亞太區 5%。

ESG 分析  
分別藉由「在 ESG議題上的曝險」和「個別公司在 ESG議題上的執行力」兩個面向來衡量公司於 ESG上的表現。 
► ESG 總分： 胡連整體的 ESG風險評級屬於中風險，於 Sustainalytics資料庫所覆蓋的公司中排名亦排行於略為領先的
位置，在汽車零組件行業中的公司中排名亦略為領先同業。 
► 在 ESG 議題上的曝險： 胡連的整體曝險屬於中等水準，處於車用零組件行業的平均水準。公司較需要改善的 ESG議
題包含商業道德、人力資源、商品治理等。 
► 個別公司在 ESG 議題上的執行力：胡連在針對重大 ESG議題的管理水準和執行力屬中等。公司已採取一些措施來管理
與重大 ESG問題相關的風險，但這些措施不足以管理其所有風險。儘管如此，該公司尚未捲入任何具有重大財務影響
的風險事件。

持有-落後同業：本中心認為根據目前股價，該檔個股基本面吸引力低於同業。此一觀點係基於本中心對該股發展前景、財務表現、利多題材、評價資訊

材、評價資訊以及風險概況之分析。建議投資人於投資部位中減持該股。 
評估中：本中心之預估、評等、目標價尚在評估中，但仍積極追蹤該個股。 
限制評等：為遵循相關法令規章及/或元大之政策，暫不給予評等及目標價。

### Page 2

2

胡連為台灣端子大廠：胡連精密股份有限公司成立於 1977 年，為台灣車用連接器
製造商，主要生產汽車端子、塑膠盒及模具等產品為主， 2Q26 產品組合為塑件
35.4%、端子 28.4%、電源配線盒(保險絲盒) 11.6%、線束 10.7%、板端件 6.1%、
高頻 5.1%、 高壓0.7%等 。 商業模式為將原物料(塑膠 、 銅等)製成端子或連接器後 ，
供貨給下游線束或模組廠，再透過線束或模組廠交貨給汽車廠商。2Q26 地區域銷
售比重：中國76%、台灣 4.7%、越南 2.7%、印尼 2.3%、歐洲 3.3%、美洲 5.1%、
亞太 5.9%。中國客戶多為 OEM 車廠，主要為大陸自有品牌車廠，1Q26 比重為
吉利 11%、比亞迪 7.4%、長安 4.1%、Lear 3.6%、奇瑞 2.6%、五菱 1%。 
2Q26 營收淡季不淡 、 逆勢衝高 ， 絕對值接近過往旺季水準：胡連 2Q26 營收 27.5
億元(+29%QoQ、+27%YoY)，達成率 112%，大幅優於預期。其中，6 月營收絕
對值來到 9.8 億元，已能與過往旺季水準並駕齊驅，表現優於市場預期。2Q26 主
要受惠中國地區揮別首季終端庫存調整、 客戶下單力道逐步回溫， 以及非中國地區
訂單需求優於預期。毛利率方面，受惠營收規模擴張，以及高附加產品比重持續提
升，有望淡化部份原物料高漲的影響，預估 2Q26 毛利率將微幅季增長。 
2H26~2027 年營收展望正向，切入模組化、智能化產品供應，胡連高附加價值產
品比重持續提升：研究處估算今年胡連新產品，如高頻、高壓、保險絲盒等將貢獻
9~10 億元(原預估 7~8 億元)，隨著新產品陸續放量，明後年量會最大，新產品毛
利率會比較高，且胡連一直積極從一般低壓線束、連接器，轉向區域化、模組化的
電線管理產品發展，預計將先切入特殊車輛之車燈域控制、座椅域控制器等，隨著
總成件產品比重增加， 也有助於均價及利潤率之提升， 有望逐步淡化原物料上漲對
毛利帶來的影響。 
中國內需市場雖然低迷，但胡連主要客戶表顯優於產業平均，且出口市場龐大，揮
別首季庫存調整後 ， 胡連中國訂單已快速回溫 ：2026 年雖中國內需車市總量承壓 ，
出口成為中國汽車產業成長核心支柱， 而胡連主要客戶為自主品牌， 其在新能源市
場和出口市場表現皆優於產業平均，參考5 月乘用車出口(含整車與 CKD）78.4 萬
輛(+75.1%YoY)，其中自主品牌出口 68.2 萬輛(+83%YoY)。受惠胡連客戶在內需
及出口市場取得強勁的表現，故揮別 1Q26 庫存調整後，胡連 2Q26 中國營收已
逐步回溫 ， 且依照中國客戶較積極的預示量 ，6~8 月營收有望逐月往上 ， 預估3Q26
營收年增上看 25%以上；而 4Q26 則迎來全年最旺季。 
非中國地區，如東南亞、歐洲市場等強勁增長及新併購機會，多元廠區分散風險：
(1) 胡連為比亞迪東南亞擴張戰略下的核心在地受惠者，在印尼取得比亞迪五款車
型的 PCB 保險絲盒訂單，隨比亞迪印尼廠產能爬坡，胡連營收認列高峰預計集中
於 4Q26 及 2027~2028 年。(2) 因應客戶分散地緣風險需求 ， 胡連於4Q26~2027
年擴大越南供貨連接器產品予美系電動車客戶， 成長幅度上看50%以上 。(3) 過去
數年胡連持續耕耘歐洲車廠，雖無立即成效，但認可車廠已逐步增加。胡連正評估
具備垂直整合效益之併購案，加速非中國市場布局。然目前併購案尚未確定，故未
納入今明年的財務預估中，故後續有上修之空間。 
在中國內需疲軟的背景下， 中國自主品牌車廠未來重心逐步轉向海外， 包含海外當
地設廠，胡連有望透過越南、印尼等，甚至歐洲新併購機會取得海外產能，提供在
地化供應服務，快速反應當地需求。 
維持買進建議 ：看好胡連憑藉積極的營收規模擴張與非中國地區比重提升， 且積極
從一般低壓連接器轉向區域化、模組化產品，隨高毛利新品於  2H26-2028 年進
入放量高峰，將有效淡化原物料成本壓力，帶動整體毛利率重回 30%以上軌道。
